title.raw: 卷二百七十九 列傳第三十八 王繼忠 傅潛 張昭允 戴興 王漢忠 王能 張凝 魏能 陳興 許均 張進 李重貴 呼延贊 劉用 耿全斌 周仁美 Volume 279 Biographies 38: Wang Jizhong, Fu Qian, Zhang Zhaoyun, Dai Xing, Wang Hanzhong, Wang Neng, Zhang Ning, Wei Neng, Chen Xing, Xu Jun, Zhang Jin, Li Zhonggui, Hu Yanzan, Liu Yong, Geng Quanbin, Zhou Renmei

sentences.zh: 王繼忠

translations.literal: Wang Jizhong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhong

sentences.zh: 王繼忠，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang Jizhong was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhong was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父充，為武騎指揮使，戍瓦橋關，卒。

translations.literal: His father Chong served as commander of the Martial Cavalry, garrisoned Waqiao Pass, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong had been commander of the Martial Cavalry and was posted to garrison Waqiao Pass, where he died in service.

sentences.zh: 繼忠年六歲，補東班殿侍。

translations.literal: When Jizhong was six years old, he was appointed an attendant of the Eastern Class in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six, Jizhong was enrolled as a palace attendant of the Eastern Class.

sentences.zh: 真宗在藩邸，得給事左右，以謹厚被親信。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was still in his princely residence, Jizhong came to serve at his side and, for his prudence and steadiness, was trusted intimately.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Zhenzong was still heir apparent, Jizhong served in his household; his careful, steadfast manner won the prince's close trust.

sentences.zh: 即位，補內殿崇班，累遷至殿前都虞候，領雲州觀察使，出為深州副都部署，改鎮、定、高陽關三路鈐轄兼河北都轉運使，遷高陽關副都部署，俄徙定州。

translations.literal: Upon his accession, Jizhong was appointed to the Inner Hall Honored Company, rose in successive promotions to chief adjutant of the Palace Front, held the nominal post of military commissioner of Yunzhou, served as deputy commander of Shenzhou, then became superintendent of the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass and concurrently chief transport commissioner of Hebei, was transferred to deputy commander of Gaoyang Pass, and soon after moved to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenzong took the throne, Jizhong entered the Inner Hall Honored Company and rose step by step to chief adjutant of the Palace Front, with the nominal title of military commissioner of Yunzhou. He was posted as deputy commander of Shenzhou, then made superintendent of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuits and chief transport commissioner for Hebei, transferred to deputy commander of Gaoyang Pass, and soon afterward reassigned to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，契丹數萬騎南侵，至望都，繼忠與大將王超及桑讚等領兵援之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Xianping era, tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen invaded south as far as Wangdu; Jizhong, together with the great general Wang Chao and Sang Zan and others, led troops to relieve the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping (1003), a Khitan force of many tens of thousands of horsemen pushed south to Wangdu. Jizhong marched to the rescue with the senior commander Wang Chao, Sang Zan, and others.

sentences.zh: 繼忠至康村，與契丹戰，自日失至乙夜，敵勢小卻。

translations.literal: Jizhong reached Kang Village and fought the Khitan from the hour of sunset until the second watch of the night, and the enemy's momentum slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At Kang Village he engaged the Khitan and fought from dusk deep into the second watch of the night, until the enemy's pressure eased slightly.

sentences.zh: 遲明復戰，繼忠陣東偏，為敵所乘，斷餉道，超、讚皆畏縮退師，竟不赴援。

translations.literal: At daybreak they fought again; Jizhong held the eastern wing of the line, was struck by the enemy, and had his supply route cut; Chao and Zan both shrank back in fear and withdrew their armies, and in the end did not come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: When battle resumed at dawn, Jizhong held the eastern wing. The enemy exploited the opening, severed his supply line, and Wang Chao and Sang Zan, both unnerved, pulled their forces back without ever coming to his relief.

sentences.zh: 繼忠獨與麾下躍馬馳赴，服飾稍異，契丹識之，圍數十重。

translations.literal: Jizhong alone, with his followers, spurred their horses forward; his dress was somewhat distinctive, the Khitan recognized him, and surrounded him in layer upon layer.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong alone charged forward with his men. His dress was distinctive enough that the Khitan recognized him and closed in with ring after ring of troops.

sentences.zh: 士皆重創，殊死戰，且戰且行，旁西山而北，至白城，遂陷於契丹。

translations.literal: His soldiers were all gravely wounded, fought to the death, advanced while fighting, skirted the western hills and went north to Baicheng, and there fell into Khitan hands.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were all badly wounded yet fought with desperate fury, fighting as they withdrew along the western hills toward the north until they reached Baicheng, where they were finally captured by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 真宗聞之震悼，初謂已死，優詔贈大同軍節度，賵賻加等，官其四子。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong heard of it he was shaken with grief; at first he believed Jizhong had died, issued a gracious edict posthumously appointing him military commissioner of Datong, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and enfeoffed his four sons.
translations.idiomatic: The news plunged Emperor Zhenzong into shock and mourning. At first he believed Jizhong had been killed, issued a gracious edict granting him the posthumous title of military commissioner of Datong, added an extra grade to the funeral gifts, and gave offices to all four of his sons.

sentences.zh: 景德初，契丹請和，令繼忠奏章，乃知其尚在。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era the Khitan sought peace and had Jizhong submit a memorial, whereupon the court learned that he was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era (1004), when the Khitan sued for peace, they had Jizhong submit a memorial on their behalf, and only then did the court learn that he was still alive.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，自是南北戢兵，繼忠有力焉。

translations.literal: The court assented, and from then on north and south laid down their arms; Jizhong had contributed force to this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and from that time the north and south ceased fighting; Jizhong had played a significant part in bringing the peace about.

sentences.zh: 歲遣使至契丹，必以襲衣、金帶、器幣、茶藥賜之，繼忠對使者亦必泣下。

translations.literal: Each year when envoys were sent to the Khitan, they invariably bestowed on him layered robes, gold belts, ritual vessels, tea, and medicines; when Jizhong met the envoys he too would always weep.
translations.idiomatic: Every year when envoys went to the Khitan court, they brought him layered robes, gold belts, ritual vessels, tea, and medicines; whenever Jizhong met the envoys he wept without fail.

sentences.zh: 嘗附表懇請召還，上以誓書約各無所求，不欲渝之，賜詔諭意。

translations.literal: He once attached a memorial earnestly begging to be recalled; the emperor, on the ground that the sworn covenant bound each side to seek nothing further, did not wish to violate it, and granted an edict explaining his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent a memorial pleading to be brought home. The emperor, citing the sworn covenant by which each side had pledged to seek nothing further from the other, was unwilling to break faith and issued an edict explaining his reasons.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遇繼忠甚厚，更其姓名為耶律顯忠，又改名宗信，封楚王，後不知其所終。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler treated Jizhong with great favor, changed his name to Yelü Xianzhong, then again to Zongxin, enfeoffed him as King of Chu, and afterward his end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler treated him with exceptional favor, gave him the Khitan name Yelü Xianzhong, later renamed him Zongxin, and enfeoffed him as King of Chu. What became of him in the end is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 子懷節、懷敏、懷德、懷政。

translations.literal: His sons were Huaijie, Huaimin, Huaide, and Huaizheng.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huaijie, Huaimin, Huaide, and Huaizheng.

sentences.zh: 真宗宮邸攀附者，繼忠之次有王守俊至濟州刺史，蔚昭敏至殿前都指揮使、保靜軍節度，翟明至洺州團練使，王遵度至磁州團練使，楊保用至西上閣門使、康州刺史，鄭懷德至御前忠佐馬步軍都軍頭、永州團練使，張承易至禮賓使，吳延昭至供備庫使，白文肇至引進使、昭州團練使，彭睿至侍衛馬軍副都指揮使、武昌軍節度，靳忠至侍衛馬軍都虞候、端州防禦使，郝榮至安國軍節度觀察留後，陳玉至冀州刺史，崔美至濟州團練使，高漢美至鄭州團練使，楊謙至御前忠佐馬步軍副都軍頭、河州刺史。

translations.literal: Among those who had attached themselves to Zhenzong's princely household, next after Jizhong were Wang Shoujun, who rose to prefect of Jizhou; Wei Zhaomin, to commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Baojing; Zhai Ming, to regimental commissioner of Mingzhou; Wang Zundu, to regimental commissioner of Cizhou; Yang Baoyong, to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and prefect of Kangzhou; Zheng Huaide, to chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse and Foot before the throne and regimental commissioner of Yongzhou; Zhang Chengyi, to commissioner of ritual guests; Wu Yanzhao, to commissioner of the supply depots; Bai Wenzhao, to introducing commissioner and regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou; Peng Rui, to deputy commander of the Imperial Horse and military commissioner of Wuchang; Jin Zhong, to adjutant of the Imperial Horse and defender of Duanzhou; Hao Rong, to acting military commissioner of Anguo; Chen Yu, to prefect of Jizhou; Cui Mei, to regimental commissioner of Jizhou; Gao Hanmei, to regimental commissioner of Zhengzhou; and Yang Qian, to deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse and Foot and prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among the men who had risen through attachment to Zhenzong's household when he was heir, the next rank after Jizhong included Wang Shoujun, who became prefect of Jizhou; Wei Zhaomin, commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Baojing; Zhai Ming, regimental commissioner of Mingzhou; Wang Zundu, regimental commissioner of Cizhou; Yang Baoyong, commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and prefect of Kangzhou; Zheng Huaide, chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse and Foot and regimental commissioner of Yongzhou; Zhang Chengyi, commissioner of ritual guests; Wu Yanzhao, commissioner of the supply depots; Bai Wenzhao, introducing commissioner and regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou; Peng Rui, deputy commander of the Imperial Horse and military commissioner of Wuchang; Jin Zhong, adjutant of the Imperial Horse and defender of Duanzhou; Hao Rong, acting military commissioner of Anguo; Chen Yu, prefect of Jizhou; Cui Mei, regimental commissioner of Jizhou; Gao Hanmei, regimental commissioner of Zhengzhou; and Yang Qian, deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse and Foot and prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 傅潛，冀州衡水人。

translations.literal: Fu Qian was a man of Hengshui in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian was a native of Hengshui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 少事州將張廷翰。

translations.literal: In youth he served the prefectural commander Zhang Tinghan.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served under the prefectural commander Zhang Tinghan.

sentences.zh: 太宗在藩邸，召置左右。

translations.literal: When Taizong was in his princely residence, he summoned Qian and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Taizong was still heir apparent, he summoned Qian into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 即位，隸殿前左班，三遷東西班指揮使。

translations.literal: Upon accession, Qian was assigned to the Left Company of the Palace Front and was thrice promoted to commander of the Eastern and Western Companies.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong took the throne, Qian was posted to the Left Company of the Palace Front and was promoted three times until he became commander of the Eastern and Western Companies.

sentences.zh: 征太原，一日，再中流矢。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan, in a single day he was struck twice by flying arrows.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Taiyuan he was hit by stray arrows twice in a single day.

sentences.zh: 又從征范陽，先到涿州，與契丹戰，生擒五百餘人。

translations.literal: He also followed the expedition against Fanyang, reached Zhuozhou first, fought the Khitan, and took more than five hundred alive.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the expedition against Fanyang, reached Zhuozhou ahead of the main force, fought the Khitan there, and took more than five hundred prisoners alive.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上過其所，見積屍及所遺器仗，嘉歎之。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor passed his position, saw the heaped corpses and abandoned weapons and armor, and praised him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor passed the battlefield, saw the piles of dead and abandoned arms and armor, and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 師旋，擢為內殿直都虞候。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Inner Hall Direct.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Inner Hall Direct.

sentences.zh: 上對樞密言：“潛從行有勞，賞薄。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Bureau of Military Affairs: "Qian followed on campaign with merit, yet his reward is thin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Bureau of Military Affairs, "Qian served on campaign with real merit, yet his reward has been meager.

sentences.zh: ”復加馬步都軍頭、領羅州刺史，改捧日右廂都指揮使、領富州團練使，遷日騎、天武左右廂都指揮使，領雲州防禦使。

translations.literal: " He was further made chief commander of the horse and foot, with nominal prefect of Luozhou, changed to commander of the Right Wing of the Sun-Bearing Guard and regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, and transferred to commander of both wings of the Day-Riding and Heavenly Martial Guards, with nominal defender of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was further appointed chief commander of the horse and foot with the nominal title of prefect of Luozhou, made commander of the Right Wing of the Sun-Bearing Guard and regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, and then transferred to command both wings of the Day-Riding and Heavenly Martial Guards with the nominal title of defender of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，命大將曹彬北征，以潛為幽州道行營前軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, the great general Cao Bin was ordered on a northern expedition, and Qian was made overall commander of horse and foot for the vanguard of the Youzhou circuit field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi (986), when the great general Cao Bin was ordered on a northern expedition, Qian was appointed overall commander of horse and foot for the vanguard of the Youzhou circuit field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師敗於拒馬河，責授右領軍衛大將軍，自檢校司徒降為右僕射，仍削功臣爵邑。

translations.literal: The army was defeated at the Juma River; he was punished by appointment as great general of the Right Army Guard, demoted from honorary Grand Preceptor to Vice Director of the Right, and still stripped of his merit noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated at the Juma River, he was demoted to great general of the Right Army Guard, reduced from honorary Grand Preceptor to Vice Director of the Right, and stripped of his merit noble rank and fief as well.

sentences.zh: 明年，起為內外馬步都軍頭、領藩州防禦使，尋拜殿前都虞候、領容州觀察使。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as chief commander of the inner and outer horse and foot, with nominal defender of Fanzhou, and soon after appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as chief commander of the inner and outer horse and foot with the nominal title of defender of Fanzhou, and soon afterward appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加殿前副都指揮使、領昭化軍節度，出為高陽關都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was made deputy commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Zhaohua, and sent out as commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong (988) he was made deputy commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Zhaohua, then posted as commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年四月，拜侍衛馬步軍都虞候、領武成軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, fourth month, he was appointed adjutant of the Imperial Horse and Foot and military commissioner of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Chunhua (991) he was appointed adjutant of the Imperial Horse and Foot and military commissioner of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 至道中，出為延州路都部署，改鎮州。

translations.literal: During the Zhidao era he was sent out as commander of the Yanzhou circuit and then transferred to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era (995–997) he was posted as commander of the Yanzhou circuit, then transferred to Zhenzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 張昭允

translations.literal: Zhang Zhaoyun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoyun

sentences.zh: 張昭允者，字仲孚，衛州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhaoyun, styled Zhongfu, was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoyun, whose style was Zhongfu, was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 以父秉蔭，試大理評事。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he was tried for the post of reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's official privilege he qualified for trial appointment as reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 潘美妻以女，奏換右班殿直，以久次，遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: Pan Mei's wife gave him her daughter in marriage; he memorialized to exchange his post for attendant of the Right Class, and through long seniority was transferred to courier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He married a daughter of Pan Mei's wife, petitioned to exchange his post for attendant of the Right Class, and after long service was promoted to courier attendant.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，契丹內擾，命為雄州監軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, when the Khitan raided within the borders, he was ordered to serve as military overseer of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong, when the Khitan raided across the border, he was appointed military overseer of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 敵騎乘秋掠境上，昭允與知州田仁朗選銳卒襲其帳，敗走之。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen took advantage of autumn to plunder the frontier; Zhaoyun, together with the prefect Tian Renlang, selected crack troops to strike their camp and routed them in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan horsemen used the autumn season to raid the frontier. Zhaoyun and the prefect Tian Renlang chose elite troops, struck their camp, and drove them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 進西上閣門副使，提總左右藏金銀錢帛。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and given overall charge of the left and right treasuries of gold, silver, cash, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and placed in overall charge of the left and right treasuries of gold, silver, cash, and silks.

sentences.zh: 昭允以諸州絹常度外長數尺，請裂取付工官備他用，歲獲羨餘。

translations.literal: Zhaoyun, noting that the silk cloth from the various prefectures regularly exceeded the standard measure by several feet, requested that the surplus be cut off and given to the craft offices for other uses, and each year obtained a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyun found that silk deliveries from the prefectures routinely ran several feet longer than the standard measure. He petitioned to have the surplus cut off and turned over to the craft offices for other uses, yielding a substantial annual surplus.

sentences.zh: 既而土卒受冬服，度之不及程，出怨言，昭允坐免官。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the soldiers received their winter clothing, the measurements fell short of the quota and they voiced complaints; Zhaoyun was punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when soldiers received their winter uniforms, the cloth fell short of the required measure and complaints erupted. Zhaoyun was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 俄起為崇儀副使，累遷西上閣門使、河西馬步軍鈐轄，屯石州。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as deputy commissioner of Honored Ceremonial, rose in successive promotions to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and superintendent of the Hexi horse and foot, and was stationed at Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as deputy commissioner of Honored Ceremonial, rose through successive promotions to commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and superintendent of the Hexi horse and foot, and was stationed at Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 會討李繼遷，王超出夏、綏州路，領後陣，超深入數百里，逾白池，道阻糧絕，昭允以所部援之，戎人大敗。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian was being attacked, Wang Chao went out by the Xia and Sui circuit route leading the rear echelon; Chao penetrated several hundred li, crossed Baichi, the road was blocked and grain exhausted, and Zhaoyun led his command to relieve him, and the barbarians were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Li Jiqian, Wang Chao marched out on the Xia and Sui circuit route at the head of the rear echelon. Chao pushed several hundred li deep, crossed Baichi, and found his line of march blocked and supplies exhausted. Zhaoyun led his troops to his relief and inflicted a crushing defeat on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 昭允喜筆劄，習射，曉音律。

translations.literal: Zhaoyun delighted in letters, practiced archery, and understood musical pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyun was fond of writing, practiced archery, and understood musical pitch.

sentences.zh: 子正中、居中。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhengzhong and Juzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhengzhong and Juzhong.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，曹彬等北征失律，諸將多坐黜免，以興為侍衛步軍都虞候，領雲州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, when Cao Bin and others failed in discipline on the northern expedition, many generals were punished by dismissal; Xing was made adjutant of the Imperial Foot and nominal defender of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi (986), when Cao Bin and others were defeated on the northern expedition and many generals were dismissed, Dai Xing was appointed adjutant of the Imperial Foot with the nominal title of defender of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹撓邊，命興屯澶州以備非常，改本州觀察使，充天雄軍副都部署。

translations.literal: When the Khitan harassed the frontier, Xing was ordered to garrison Chunzhou against emergencies, was changed to military commissioner of his home prefecture, and served as deputy commander of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan harassed the frontier, he was ordered to garrison Chunzhou against emergencies, made military commissioner of his home prefecture, and appointed deputy commander of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷步軍都指揮使、領鎮武軍節度，賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to commander of the Foot, with military commissioner of Zhenwu, and was granted layered robes, a gold belt, and saddled horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was made commander of the Foot and military commissioner of Zhenwu, and was granted layered robes, a gold belt, and saddled horses.

sentences.zh: 曆澶州，天雄軍都部署，改殿前副都指揮使，出帥鎮、定二州。

translations.literal: He served at Chunzhou and as commander of the Tianxiong army, was changed to deputy commander of the Palace Front, and went out as commander-in-chief of Zhen and Ding prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander at Chunzhou and of the Tianxiong army, was made deputy commander of the Palace Front, and went out as commander-in-chief of Zhen and Ding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊群起，會五巡檢兵討之，逾月不能克。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in groups; the troops of the five inspection circuits were assembled to attack them, yet for more than a month they could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere. Troops from the five inspection circuits were assembled to suppress them, but for more than a month they could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 興陰勒所部潛出擊之，擒戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Xing secretly ordered his command to slip out and strike them, capturing and killing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Xing secretly ordered his troops to slip out and strike them, capturing and killing nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙高陽關，遷殿前都指揮使，領定國軍節度，賜白金萬兩，歲加給錢七百萬。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Gaoyang Pass, promoted to commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Dingguo, granted ten thousand taels of white gold, and given an additional seven million cash per year.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Gaoyang Pass, promoted to commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Dingguo, granted ten thousand taels of white gold, and given an additional seven million cash per year.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，出為定武軍節度，歲加給錢千萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was sent out as military commissioner of Dingwu, with an additional ten million cash per year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua (994) he was posted as military commissioner of Dingwu, with an additional ten million cash granted each year.

sentences.zh: 西北未平，徙夏州路行營都部署、知州事。

translations.literal: As the northwest was not yet pacified, he was transferred to commander of the Xiazhou circuit field headquarters and acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: With the northwest still unsettled, he was transferred to commander of the Xiazhou circuit field headquarters and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 時五路討李繼遷，興所部深入千餘里，不見賊。

translations.literal: At the time five routes were campaigning against Li Jiqian; Xing's command penetrated more than a thousand li deep and did not see the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time five routes were campaigning against Li Jiqian. Xing's command pushed more than a thousand li into enemy territory without ever encountering the rebels.

sentences.zh: 會太宗崩，三上表求赴國哀，不俟報上道。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, he thrice submitted memorials begging to attend the national mourning and, without waiting for a reply, set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong died, he submitted three memorials begging to attend the national mourning and, without waiting for a reply, set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 及至京師，以擅離所部，左遷左領衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, for leaving his post without authorization he was demoted to senior general of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he was demoted to senior general of the Left Army Guard for leaving his post without authorization.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，兼判左金吾街仗，俄出知京兆府，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was additionally assigned to judge the Left Golden Crow Street Guard, and soon after was sent out as prefect of Jingzhao and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was additionally assigned to judge the Left Golden Crow Street Guard, was soon afterward posted as prefect of Jingzhao, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，遣中使護其喪歸葬鄉里。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, and a palace envoy was sent to escort his coffin home for burial in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor, and a palace envoy was dispatched to escort his coffin home for burial in his native district.

sentences.zh: 錄其子永和、永豐。

translations.literal: His sons Yonghe and Yongfeng were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yonghe and Yongfeng were given offices.

sentences.zh: 王漢忠

translations.literal: Wang Hanzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hanzhong

sentences.zh: 五年，罷西面經略使，命漢忠為邠寧、環慶兩路都部署，李允正、宋沆為鈐轄，領戍兵二萬五千人，委漢忠分道控制。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the western frontier commissioner was abolished; Hanzhong was ordered as commander of the Binning and Huanqing circuits, with Li Yunzheng and Song Hong as superintendents, leading twenty-five thousand garrison troops, and Hanzhong was entrusted to control them by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the western frontier commissioner was abolished. Hanzhong was appointed commander of the Binning and Huanqing circuits, with Li Yunzheng and Song Hong as superintendents, in charge of twenty-five thousand garrison troops divided among separate routes under his overall control.

sentences.zh: 數月召還，坐違詔無功，責為左屯衛上將軍、出知襄州，常奉外增歲給錢二百萬。

translations.literal: After several months he was recalled; for violating the edict without achievement he was punished as senior general of the Left Garrison Guard and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou, with an additional two million cash per year beyond his regular salary.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was recalled. For defying the edict and achieving nothing he was demoted to senior general of the Left Garrison Guard and posted as prefect of Xiangzhou, with an additional two million cash per year beyond his regular salary.

sentences.zh: 未上道，暴得疾卒。

translations.literal: Before he had set out on the road he suddenly fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out he was stricken by sudden illness and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，以其長子內殿崇班從吉為閣門祗候，次子從政、從益為左右侍禁。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his eldest son Congji of the Inner Hall Honored Company was made gate attendant, and his second sons Congzheng and Congyi were made attendants of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor. His eldest son Congji of the Inner Hall Honored Company was made gate attendant, and his younger sons Congzheng and Congyi were made attendants of the Left and Right.

sentences.zh: 漢忠有識略，軍政甚肅，每行師，詰旦，必行香祝曰：“願軍民無犯吾令，違者一毫不貸。

translations.literal: Hanzhong had strategic insight; military administration under him was very strict. Whenever he took the field, at dawn he would burn incense and pray: "May soldiers and civilians alike not violate my orders; those who do shall not be spared in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong was a man of strategic insight and ran an exceptionally strict military administration. Whenever he took the field, at dawn he burned incense and prayed: "May soldiers and civilians alike not violate my orders; those who do shall not be spared in the slightest.

sentences.zh: ”故所部無盜。

translations.literal: " Therefore under his command there were no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Under his command there were accordingly no bandits.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，不務小節，輕財樂施。

translations.literal: In nature he was firm and resolute, did not trouble over small points, and was light with wealth and glad to give.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm and resolute by nature, cared little for minor proprieties, and was generous with his wealth.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，頗能詩。

translations.literal: He loved reading books and was quite able in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to read and was a capable poet.

sentences.zh: 喜儒士，待賓佐有禮，名稱甚茂，以是自矜尚，群帥不悅。

translations.literal: He delighted in Confucian scholars and treated his staff with courtesy; his reputation was very flourishing, and because of this he prided himself, and the commanders were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in scholars and treated his staff with courtesy. His reputation was widely celebrated, but this self-regard won him little favor among his fellow commanders.

sentences.zh: 漢忠沒後，其子從吉詣闕上書訟父冤，因歷詆群臣有行賂樹黨及蒙蔽邊防屯戍艱苦之事。

translations.literal: After Hanzhong's death his son Congji came to court and submitted a memorial pleading his father's wrong, and in the course of it denounced one after another the ministers for bribery, faction-building, and concealing the hardships of frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanzhong's death his son Congji came to court with a memorial pleading his father's wrong, denouncing in turn various ministers for bribery, faction-building, and concealing the hardships of frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 真宗命樞密王繼英等問狀，從吉止誦狀中語，他無所對。

translations.literal: Zhenzong ordered Wang Jiying of the Bureau of Military Affairs and others to examine the case; Congji could only recite the words of the memorial and had no other answers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong ordered Wang Jiying of the Bureau of Military Affairs and others to examine the case. Congji could only recite the words of his memorial and had nothing further to say.

sentences.zh: 上以從吉付御史，具伏，乃進士楊逢為之辭。

translations.literal: The emperor handed Congji over to the censorate; he confessed everything, and it turned out that the jinshi Yang Feng had composed the text for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed Congji over to the censorate. He confessed fully, and it emerged that a jinshi named Yang Feng had drafted the memorial for him.

sentences.zh: 從吉坐除名，配隨州；

translations.literal: Congji was punished by removal from the rolls and exile to Suizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Congji was struck from the rolls and exiled to Suizhou;

sentences.zh: 逢杖配春州。

translations.literal: Feng was beaten with the staff and exiled to Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was flogged and exiled to Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗詢軍校勤勇者，委以方面，因語宰相曰：“聞王能、魏能頗宣力公家，陳興、張禹珪亦有聲於時，才固難全，拔十得五，亦有助也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhenzong inquired among military officers for the diligent and brave to entrust with regional command, he said to the chief ministers: "I have heard that Wang Neng and Wei Neng exert themselves greatly for the state, and Chen Xing and Zhang Yugui also have reputation in their time; talent is hard to find in full measure, yet if from ten one obtains five, that too is of help.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Zhenzong was looking among military officers for diligent, brave men to entrust with regional command, he told the chief ministers: "I have heard that Wang Neng and Wei Neng serve the state with real force, and that Chen Xing and Zhang Yugui also enjoy strong reputations. Talent is never found in full measure, but if from ten candidates one obtains five who are sound, that is help enough.

sentences.zh: ”景德初，擢本州防禦使，與魏能、張凝並命出為邢洺路都部署，俄改鎮、定、高陽關三路行營都部署、押策先鋒。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Jingde, Neng was promoted to defender of his home prefecture, and together with Wei Neng and Zhang Ning was appointed commander of the Xing and Mo circuit; soon after he was changed to commander of the field headquarters of the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass and commander of the vanguard of the assault corps.
translations.idiomatic: " Early in the Jingde era (1004), Wang Neng was promoted to defender of his home prefecture and, together with Wei Neng and Zhang Ning, appointed commander of the Xing and Mo circuit. He was soon transferred to commander of the field headquarters for the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuits and commander of the vanguard of the assault corps.

sentences.zh: 護城祁州，躬率丁夫，旦暮不離役所，宴犒周洽。

translations.literal: He fortified Qizhou, personally led the corvée laborers, morning and evening never leaving the work site, and feasted and rewarded them with full generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Qizhou, personally led the corvée laborers, and from dawn to dusk never left the worksite, feasting and rewarding the men with generous care.

sentences.zh: 會詔使自北至者言之，手詔褒飭，連徙天雄軍、高陽關二部署，改定州副都部署。

translations.literal: When an edict envoy coming from the north reported this, an autograph edict praised and encouraged him; he was transferred in succession to the two commands of the Tianxiong army and Gaoyang Pass, and was changed to deputy commander of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy returning from the north reported his conduct, the emperor sent an autograph edict of praise. Neng was transferred in succession to command the Tianxiong army and Gaoyang Pass, then made deputy commander of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，詔合鎮、定兩路部署為一，命能領之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict merged the commands of the Zhen and Ding circuits into one and ordered Neng to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1009), an edict merged the commands of the Zhen and Ding circuits into one and placed Neng in charge.

sentences.zh: 明年召入，拜侍衛步軍副都指揮使、領曹州觀察使。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled and appointed deputy commander of the Imperial Foot and military commissioner of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to court and appointed deputy commander of the Imperial Foot and military commissioner of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，留為京城巡檢兼留司殿前司事。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were performed at Fenyin, he was left behind as capital inspector and concurrently in charge of Palace Front affairs during the emperor's absence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the Fenyin sacrifices, Neng was left behind as capital inspector and placed in charge of Palace Front affairs during the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 禮成，加領振武軍節度，復為鎮、定副都部署兼知定州。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he was additionally made military commissioner of Zhenwu, and again served as deputy commander of Zhen and Ding and acting prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, he was additionally made military commissioner of Zhenwu and again posted as deputy commander of Zhen and Ding and acting prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，表求入覲，許之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he submitted a memorial requesting an audience and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he petitioned for an audience at court and was granted permission.

sentences.zh: 先是，節帥陛見，必飲於長春殿，掌兵者則不預。

translations.literal: Previously, when military commissioners had audience at court they were always given drink in the Ever-Spring Hall, but those who held military command were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when military commissioners had audience at court they were always entertained in the Ever-Spring Hall, but commanders who held active military posts were not included.

sentences.zh: 至是，特令用藩臣例。

translations.literal: On this occasion he was specially ordered to follow the precedent for regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he was specially granted the treatment accorded to regional lords.

sentences.zh: 有司言：“能既赴坐，則殿前馬軍帥皆當侍立。

translations.literal: The responsible offices said: "Since Neng has taken his seat, the commanders of the Palace Front horse should all stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices said: "Since Neng has been seated, the commanders of the Palace Front horse ought all to stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: ”由是特令諸帥預坐，自是掌兵者率以為例。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the various commanders were specially ordered to take seats in advance, and from then on those who held military command generally took this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the various commanders were specially ordered to take seats as well, and from then on commanders who held active military posts generally followed this precedent.

sentences.zh: 俄還屯所，改領靜江軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his garrison post and was changed to military commissioner of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his garrison and was made military commissioner of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，轉都指揮使、領保靜軍節度。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi he was transferred to commander and military commissioner of Baojing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi (1017) he was transferred to commander and military commissioner of Baojing.

sentences.zh: 是冬代還，入見，以足疾免舞蹈，賜宴。

translations.literal: That winter, when his term ended and he returned, he had audience; for foot ailment he was excused from the ritual dance and granted a feast.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when his tour of duty ended and he returned to court, he was granted an audience. Because of a foot ailment he was excused from the ritual dance and given a feast.

sentences.zh: 累表求解，特與告醫療。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials requesting release from office and was specially granted leave for medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to resign and was specially granted leave for medical treatment.

sentences.zh: 二年，制授彰信軍節度，罷軍職赴鎮，以地近其鄉里，寵之也。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed by decree military commissioner of Zhangxin, relinquished his military post and went to his commandery, because the place was near his native district — a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed by decree military commissioner of Zhangxin, relinquished his military post, and went to his commandery — a mark of favor, since the post lay near his home district.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: The next year he died, at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，而錄其子守信等官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, and his son Shouxin and others were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor, and his son Shouxin and others were given offices.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，以其有材幹，與王斌、王憲並授洛苑使，凝領繡州刺史，賜襲衣、金帶，每頒賚必異等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, because of his ability, together with Wang Bin and Wang Xian he was appointed commissioner of the Luoyuan, with Ning holding nominal prefect of Xiuzhou; layered robes and a gold belt were granted, and whenever gifts were distributed he always received a higher grade.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua (990), Zhang Ning's ability won him appointment, together with Wang Bin and Wang Xian, as commissioner of the Luoyuan, with the nominal title of prefect of Xiuzhou. He was granted layered robes and a gold belt, and whenever gifts were distributed he always received a higher grade than the rest.

sentences.zh: 出為天雄軍駐泊都監，移貝州，改高陽關行營鈐轄、六宅使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as garrison overseer of the Tianxiong army, transferred to Beizhou, and changed to superintendent of the Gaoyang Pass field headquarters and commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as garrison overseer of the Tianxiong army, transferred to Beizhou, and made superintendent of the Gaoyang Pass field headquarters and commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 真宗踐祚，加莊宅使，遷北作坊使。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Ning was made commissioner of the Manor Estates and transferred to commissioner of the Northern Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Ning was made commissioner of the Manor Estates and transferred to commissioner of the Northern Workshops.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，契丹南侵，凝率所部兵設伏於瀛州西，出其不意，腹背奮擊，挺身陷敵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, when the Khitan invaded south, Ning led his troops to set an ambush west of Yingzhou, struck them unawares, attacked from front and rear with full force, and threw himself into the enemy ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping, when the Khitan invaded south, Ning led his command in an ambush west of Yingzhou, took them by surprise, struck from front and rear with full force, and plunged personally into the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 凝子昭遠，年十六，從行。

translations.literal: Ning's son Zhaoyuan, sixteen years old, followed on the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoyuan, sixteen years old, accompanied him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 即單騎疾呼，突入陣中，掖凝出，左右披靡不敢動。

translations.literal: He immediately spurred his horse alone with urgent cries, burst into the battle line, supported Ning out, and those to left and right fell back in awe and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse forward alone with urgent cries, burst into the battle line, pulled his father clear, and the enemy on either side fell back in awe and dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹兵大至，車駕幸大名，凝與范廷召於莫州東分據要害，斷其歸路。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan army came in great force and the imperial carriage went to Daming; Ning and Fan Tingzhao took key positions east of Mozhou and cut off their route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a great Khitan army advanced and the emperor went to Daming. Ning and Fan Tingzhao seized key positions east of Mozhou and cut off the enemy's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 契丹宵遁，凝縱兵擊之，盡奪所掠生口、資畜。

translations.literal: The Khitan fled by night; Ning loosed his troops upon them and recovered all the people and livestock they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan fled by night. Ning loosed his troops in pursuit and recovered all the captives and livestock they had taken.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮、定、高陽關路前陣鈐轄，遷趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to superintendent of the vanguard of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuit and promoted to prefect of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of the vanguard for the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuit and promoted to prefect of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，召還，代潘璘為邠寧環慶靈州路副部署兼安撫使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled and replaced Pan Lin as deputy commander and pacification commissioner of the Binning, Huanqing, and Lingzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled to replace Pan Lin as deputy commander and pacification commissioner of the Binning, Huanqing, and Lingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 時斥堠數擾，轉運使劉綜懼飛免不給，問計於凝。

translations.literal: At the time the scouts were repeatedly harassed; the transport commissioner Liu Zong feared that relay horses could not keep supplies flowing and asked Ning for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts were being harassed repeatedly. Transport commissioner Liu Zong feared that relay couriers could not keep supplies moving and asked Ning for advice.

sentences.zh: 凝曰：“今當深入，因敵資糧，不足慮也。

translations.literal: Ning said: "We should now penetrate deep and live off enemy grain; there is no need for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, "We should push deep into enemy territory now and live off their supplies. There is no need to worry.

sentences.zh: ”乃自白豹鎮率兵入敵境，生擒賊將，燒蕩三百餘帳、芻糧八萬，斬首五千餘，獲牛馬、器甲二萬，降九百餘人。

translations.literal: " He then led troops from Baibao town into enemy territory, captured enemy generals alive, burned more than three hundred camps and eighty thousand bundles of fodder, beheaded more than five thousand, seized twenty thousand head of cattle and horses and sets of armor, and accepted the surrender of more than nine hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led troops from Baibao town into enemy territory, captured rebel generals alive, burned more than three hundred camps and eighty thousand bundles of fodder, beheaded more than five thousand men, seized twenty thousand head of cattle and horses and sets of armor, and accepted the surrender of more than nine hundred people.

sentences.zh: 慶州蕃族胡家門等桀黠難制，凝因襲破之。

translations.literal: The Hu family gate and other clans of the Fan people of Qingzhou were crafty and hard to control; Ning took advantage to strike and break them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu family gate and other Qingzhou Fan clans were crafty and hard to control. Ning struck them by surprise and broke their power.

sentences.zh: 又熟戶與生羌錯居，頗為誘脅，凝引兵至八州原、分水嶺、柔遠鎮，降峇<者多>等百七十餘族，合四千戶，邊境獲安。

translations.literal: Moreover, registered households and raw Qiang lived intermixed and were much enticed and coerced; Ning led troops to Bazhou Plain, Watershed Ridge, and Rouyuan town, and the Ba duo and more than one hundred seventy other clans submitted, totaling four thousand households, and the frontier was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Registered households and raw Qiang also lived intermixed and were much subject to enticement and coercion. Ning led troops to Bazhou Plain, Watershed Ridge, and Rouyuan town and received the submission of the Ba duo and more than one hundred seventy other clans, totaling four thousand households, and the frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 就加寧州團練使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally made regimental commissioner of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon additionally made regimental commissioner of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，遷本州防禦使，代楊嗣為定州路行營副部署，徙保州駐泊，又兼北面安撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was transferred to defender of his home prefecture, replaced Yang Si as deputy commander of the Dingzhou circuit field headquarters, moved to garrison at Baozhou, and was additionally made northern frontier pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he was made defender of his home prefecture, replaced Yang Si as deputy commander of the Dingzhou circuit field headquarters, posted to garrison Baozhou, and additionally made northern frontier pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時王超為總帥，以大兵頓中山，朝議擇凝與魏能、田敏、楊延昭分握精騎，俟契丹至，則深入以牽其勢。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chao was overall commander with the main force encamped at Zhongshan; the court chose Ning, together with Wei Neng, Tian Min, and Yang Yanzhao, each to command elite cavalry, so that when the Khitan arrived they could penetrate deep and pull at the enemy's momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao was then overall commander with the main army encamped at Zhongshan. The court chose Ning, Wei Neng, Tian Min, and Yang Yanzhao each to command elite cavalry so that when the Khitan arrived they could strike deep and pull at the enemy's momentum.

sentences.zh: 超嘗請四人悉隸所部，上以本設奇兵撓敵之心腹，若復取裁大將，則無以責效，乃令凝等不受超節度。

translations.literal: Chao once requested that all four be placed under his command; the emperor said that these irregular troops had been set up to strike at the enemy's vitals, and if they were again subject to the great commander's discretion there would be no way to demand results, and therefore ordered that Ning and the others not be under Chao's command.
translations.idiomatic: Chao once asked that all four be placed under his command. The emperor replied that these irregular forces had been set up to strike at the enemy's vitals; if they were again subject to the great commander's discretion there would be no way to demand results. He therefore ordered that Ning and the others not answer to Chao.

sentences.zh: 時魏能逗撓，退保城堡，眾皆憤悱，責讓能，凝獨默然。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Neng was dilatory and held back, retreating to guard castles and forts; all were indignant and reproached Neng, but Ning alone remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Neng was then dilatory and held back, retreating to guard castles and forts. The others were indignant and reproached him, but Ning alone remained silent.

sentences.zh: 或問之，凝曰：“能粗材險愎，既不為諸君所容，吾復切言之，使其心不自安，非計也。

translations.literal: When someone asked him, Ning said: "Neng is a coarse talent, fierce and obstinate; since he is already not tolerated by you gentlemen, if I speak sharply again and make his heart ill at ease, that is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Ning said, "Neng is a coarse, obstinate man. Since the rest of you already cannot abide him, if I speak sharply again and unsettle his mind, that is no good plan.

sentences.zh: ”上聞而嘉其有識。

translations.literal: " When the emperor heard of this he praised his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard this he praised his discernment.

sentences.zh: 車駕觀兵澶淵，凝率眾抵易州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reviewed troops at Chanyuan, Ning led his forces to reach Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reviewed troops at Chanyuan, Ning led his forces to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹受盟北歸，所過猶侵剽不已，遂以凝為緣邊安撫使，提兵躡其後，契丹乃不敢略奪。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Khitan accepted the treaty and returned north, they still raided and plundered along the way without cease; Ning was therefore made frontier pacification commissioner, led troops in their tracks, and the Khitan then did not dare seize and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan accepted the treaty and returned north they still raided along the way without cease. Ning was made frontier pacification commissioner and led troops in their tracks until the Khitan no longer dared to plunder.

sentences.zh: 改高陽關部署。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 明年議勞，就加殿前都虞候，卒。

translations.literal: The next year, when merits were discussed, he was additionally made chief adjutant of the Palace Front and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when merits were discussed, he was additionally made chief adjutant of the Palace Front and died in office.

sentences.zh: 凝忠勇好功名，累任西北，善訓士卒，繕完器仗，前後賞賜多以犒師，家無餘資，京師無居第。

translations.literal: Ning was loyal and brave and loved reputation; he served repeatedly in the northwest, was skilled at training soldiers and repairing weapons and armor, and most rewards before and after were used to reward the troops; his household had no surplus wealth and he had no residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was loyal and brave and loved reputation. He served repeatedly in the northwest, trained soldiers well, kept weapons and armor in good repair, and spent most of his rewards on his troops. His household had no surplus wealth and he owned no house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 真宗悼惜之，贈彰德軍節度，遣中使護喪還京，官給葬事，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: Zhenzong mourned him, posthumously made him military commissioner of Zhangde, sent a palace envoy to escort the coffin back to the capital, provided official funeral arrangements, and gave generous relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong mourned him, posthumously made him military commissioner of Zhangde, sent a palace envoy to escort the coffin to the capital, provided an official funeral, and gave generous relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 子昭遠。

translations.literal: His son was Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 魏能，鄆人也。

translations.literal: Wei Neng was a man of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Neng was a native of Yun prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少應募，隸雲騎軍，後選補日騎左射，又隸殿前班，七遷散員左班都知。

translations.literal: In youth he answered the recruitment call, was assigned to the Cloud Cavalry, was later selected and appointed to the Left Archers of the Day-Riding, then assigned to the Palace Front company, and was promoted seven times to commander of the Left Company of the Unattached.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he enlisted, was assigned to the Cloud Cavalry, was later selected for the Left Archers of the Day-Riding, then posted to the Palace Front company, and rose through seven promotions to commander of the Left Company of the Unattached.

sentences.zh: 舊制，諸軍辭見，才器勇敢或迥異出群者，許將校交舉以任，使毋枉其志。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when the various armies took leave for audience, those of talent, courage, or markedly outstanding ability were permitted to be recommended for appointment by their officers so that their ambitions would not be thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, when troops from the various armies came to court for audience, men of talent, courage, or markedly outstanding ability could be recommended for appointment by their officers so that their ambitions would not be thwarted.

sentences.zh: 能時戍外藩，咸未有舉者。

translations.literal: Neng was then garrisoned on the outer frontier and none had recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Neng was then garrisoned on the outer frontier and no one had recommended him.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：“能材勇過人，朕可自保。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Neng's talent and courage surpass other men; I can rely on him myself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "Neng's talent and courage surpass other men. I can rely on him myself.

sentences.zh: ”由是進用之。

translations.literal: " From this he was advanced and employed.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time he was promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，加御前忠佐馬軍副都軍頭，歷殿前左班都虞候、領溪州刺史，加秩轉馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he was made deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne, served successively as adjutant of the Left Company of the Palace Front and nominal prefect of Xizhou, was raised in rank and transferred to chief commander of the horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he was made deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne, served as adjutant of the Left Company of the Palace Front and nominal prefect of Xizhou, was raised in rank, and transferred to chief commander of the horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，真拜黃州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he was formally appointed prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was formally appointed prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，為鎮、定、高陽關三路前陣鈐轄。

translations.literal: The next year he was made superintendent of the vanguard of the three circuits of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made superintendent of the vanguard of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuits.

sentences.zh: 五年，知鄭州團練使，復任威虜軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made acting regimental commissioner of Zhengzhou and again placed in command of the Weilu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made acting regimental commissioner of Zhengzhou and again placed in command of the Weilu army.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，能當城西，與諸將合戰，無憚色，大敗其眾，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, Neng held the western side of the city, joined the other generals in battle without fear, and greatly defeated their force, beheading twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, Neng held the western side of the city, fought alongside the other generals without fear, and inflicted a crushing defeat, beheading twenty thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 契丹統軍鐵林相公來薄陣，能發矢殪之，並其將十五人，奪甲馬、兵械益眾。

translations.literal: The Khitan commander-in-chief, the Iron Forest Duke, came to press the line; Neng loosed an arrow and killed him, together with fifteen of his officers, and seized armor, horses, and weapons in still greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan commander-in-chief, the Iron Forest Duke, pressed the line. Neng shot him dead with an arrow, together with fifteen of his officers, and seized armor, horses, and weapons in still greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 契丹復入，能率州軍逆戰南關門，遣其子正與都監劉知訓間道絕敵行勢，戰數十合，退薄西山下，破走之，獲器甲十八萬。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded again, Neng led the prefectural troops to meet them in battle at the South Gate, sent his son Zheng and the overseer Liu Zhixun by a side path to cut off the enemy's movement, fought several dozen engagements, retreated pressed against the western hills, broke them and drove them off, and seized one hundred eighty thousand sets of armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded again, Neng led the prefectural troops to meet them at the South Gate, sent his son Zheng and overseer Liu Zhixun by a side path to cut off the enemy's movement, fought several dozen engagements, withdrew pressed against the western hills, broke the enemy and drove them off, and seized one hundred eighty thousand sets of armor.

sentences.zh: 契丹嘗謀入鈔，能偵知，即發兵逆擊，生擒酋帥，殄滅殆盡。

translations.literal: The Khitan once plotted to enter for raiding; Neng detected it, immediately sent troops to strike them in advance, captured their chieftain alive, and exterminated them nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan once plotted a raiding incursion. Neng detected it, immediately sent troops to strike them in advance, captured their chieftain alive, and exterminated them nearly to the last man.

sentences.zh: 六年，改威虜軍部署、知軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to commander of the Weilu army and given charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made commander of the Weilu army with charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 士民詣闕下乞留能，詔嘉之。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians went to court to beg that Neng be retained, and an edict praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians went to court to beg that Neng be retained, and an edict praised their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 能建言戍卒逸邊境者，請沒其妻與子為奴婢。

translations.literal: Neng proposed that for garrison soldiers who fled across the border, their wives and children be confiscated as male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Neng proposed that garrison soldiers who fled across the border should have their wives and children confiscated as slaves.

sentences.zh: 上慮嚴迫，聽緩期自新，違以法坐。

translations.literal: The emperor feared the measure was too harsh, permitted a grace period for reform, and punished violations according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the measure was too harsh, allowed a grace period for reform, and punished violations according to law.

sentences.zh: 會浚順安軍營田河道以扼寇，徙莫州路部署。

translations.literal: When the Shun'an army's garrison-farm canals were being dredged to check the enemy, he was transferred to commander of the Mozhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shun'an army's garrison-farm canals were being dredged to check the enemy, he was transferred to commander of the Mozhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 石普屯兵順安之西境，詔能與楊延昭、田敏掎角為備。

translations.literal: Shi Pu encamped his troops on the western border of Shun'an; an edict ordered Neng, together with Yang Yanzhao and Tian Min, to support each other in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu encamped on the western border of Shun'an. An edict ordered Neng, Yang Yanzhao, and Tian Min to support each other in readiness.

sentences.zh: 景德初，破敵長城口，追越陽山，斬首級、獲兵器益眾，詔賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he broke the enemy at Changcheng Pass, pursued beyond Yang Mountain, beheaded many and seized weapons in still greater numbers, and was issued an edict gifts of brocade robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he broke the enemy at Changcheng Pass, pursued beyond Yang Mountain, took many heads and seized weapons in still greater numbers, and was granted brocade robes and a gold belt by edict.

sentences.zh: 復以所部禦寇於順安。

translations.literal: He again used his command to defend against the enemy at Shun'an.
translations.idiomatic: He again used his command to defend against the enemy at Shun'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，召拜防禦使，復出為寧邊軍路部署。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was recalled and appointed defender, and again sent out as commander of the Ningbian circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was recalled and appointed defender, then again sent out as commander of the Ningbian circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔推能果略，再任以威虜，使副精兵伺敵動止。

translations.literal: An edict commended Neng's resolution and resourcefulness, again entrusted him with the Weilu army, and had him lead elite troops to watch the enemy's movements.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Neng's resolution and resourcefulness, again entrusted him with the Weilu army, and had him lead elite troops to watch the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 邊人百餘掠居民，樹蕃僧為帥，能與田敏、楊勳合兵設伏擊之，擒其帥。

translations.literal: More than a hundred frontier people plundered civilians and set up a Fan monk as leader; Neng, together with Tian Min and Yang Xun, combined forces, set an ambush, struck them, and captured their leader.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred frontier people plundered civilians and set up a Fan monk as leader. Neng, Tian Min, and Yang Xun combined forces, set an ambush, struck them, and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 賊來逼城，能出兵拒之，少衄，即卻陣入城，張凝以兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: When bandits came pressing the city, Neng led troops to resist them, suffered a slight setback, then withdrew his line into the city; Zhang Ning used troops to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits pressed the city, Neng led troops to resist, suffered a slight setback, withdrew into the city, and Zhang Ning drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 會詔能與凝領偏師分道入幽、易，牽制契丹之勢，能畏愞不前，且不戢所部，多俘奪人馬。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered Neng and Ning to lead detached columns by separate routes into You and Yi to check the Khitan's momentum, Neng, fearful and timid, did not advance, and moreover did not restrain his command, seizing many people, horses, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered Neng and Ning to lead detached columns by separate routes into You and Yi to check the Khitan's momentum, Neng, fearful and timid, would not advance and failed to restrain his men, who seized many people, horses, and goods.

sentences.zh: 俄徙屯定州，及遣凝躡跡北行，能粗險，自度無功，心愧，多怨辭，以訕聞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison at Dingzhou; when Ning was sent to follow their tracks north, Neng was coarse and dangerous, judged himself without achievement, felt ashamed in heart, uttered many complaints, and his slander reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to garrison at Dingzhou. When Ning was sent to follow the enemy's tracks north, Neng was coarse and dangerous by nature, judged that he himself had achieved nothing, felt ashamed, uttered many complaints, and his slander reached the court.

sentences.zh: 朝議謂能剛猾少檢，不可專任，乃命綦政敏為鈐轄，俾同職焉。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Neng was obstinate, cunning, and lacking in restraint and could not be solely entrusted; Qi Zhengmin was therefore appointed superintendent so that they might share the duty.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Neng was obstinate, cunning, and lacking in restraint and could not be solely entrusted. Qi Zhengmin was therefore appointed superintendent so that they might share the duty.

sentences.zh: 明年，師還大名。

translations.literal: The next year the army returned to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the army returned to Daming.

sentences.zh: 時王能、曹璨各領兵歸闕，即城下，鈐轄孫全照遣能、璨之師由北門分道先入，能師繼之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Neng and Cao Shen each led troops returning to court and reached the foot of the city wall; superintendent Sun Quanzhao sent the armies of Neng and Shen in by the north gate by separate routes to enter first, and Neng's army followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Neng and Cao Shen each led troops returning to court and reached the foot of the wall. Superintendent Sun Quanzhao sent their armies in first by the north gate by separate routes, and Neng's army followed.

sentences.zh: 能怒全照之後己，即疾驅競入，全照射之，能嚄唶不堪，奪全照弓以去。

translations.literal: Neng was angry that Quanzhao had placed him behind, immediately spurred his horse in a racing entry; Quanzhao shot at him, Neng roared and raged unbearably, and seized Quanzhao's bow and left.
translations.idiomatic: Neng was angry that Quanzhao had placed him behind and spurred his horse in a racing entry. Quanzhao shot at him. Neng roared in fury, seized Quanzhao's bow, and rode off.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詣判府王欽若誣全照射傷押隊閣門楊凝，詞頗紛競。

translations.literal: The next day he went to the administrative prefect Wang Qinruo and falsely accused Quanzhao of shooting and wounding the gate attendant Yang Ning who was escorting the column; the words were much disputed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he went to administrative prefect Wang Qinruo and falsely accused Quanzhao of shooting and wounding column escort Yang Ning. The dispute was bitter.

sentences.zh: 全照密疏能摧兵退縮，師緩失期，及師旋不整狀。

translations.literal: Quanzhao submitted a secret memorial that Neng had crushed his troops in retreat, slowed the army and missed the deadline, and that on the army's return his ranks were not in order.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao submitted a secret memorial charging that Neng had crushed his troops in retreat, slowed the army and missed the deadline, and returned with his ranks in disorder.

sentences.zh: 上初聞能逗遛，微怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor first heard that Neng had been dilatory he was slightly angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first heard that Neng had been dilatory he was slightly angry.

sentences.zh: 會全照奏，乃質實於張凝、白守素等，即責授右羽林將軍，出為鞏縣都監。

translations.literal: When Quanzhao's memorial arrived the facts were verified through Zhang Ning, Bai Shousu, and others; Neng was immediately punished by appointment as general of the Right Feathered Forest and sent out as overseer of Gong county.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhao's memorial arrived the charges were verified through Zhang Ning, Bai Shousu, and others. Neng was demoted to general of the Right Feathered Forest and sent out as overseer of Gong county.

sentences.zh: 明年，以自陳，特改官右驍衛大將軍、虢州都監，累遷加領康州團練使。

translations.literal: The next year, on his own petition, he was specially changed to great general of the Right Valiant Cavalry and overseer of Guo prefecture, and in successive promotions was additionally made regimental commissioner of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on his own petition, he was specially changed to great general of the Right Valiant Cavalry and overseer of Guo prefecture, and in successive promotions was additionally made regimental commissioner of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.

sentences.zh: 錄其子正為閣門祗候，靖為三班奉職。

translations.literal: His son Zheng was enrolled as gate attendant and Jing as third-class attendant on duty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng was enrolled as gate attendant and Jing as third-class attendant on duty.

sentences.zh: 陳興，澶州衛南人。

translations.literal: Chen Xing was a man of Weinan in Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xing was a native of Weinan in Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中應募為卒，得隸禦龍右直。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era he answered the recruitment call as a soldier and was assigned to the Right Direct of the Imperial Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he enlisted as a soldier and was assigned to the Right Direct of the Imperial Dragon.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，幸幽陵，興常從，特被賞賜，累遷天武指揮使。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned in Hedong and visited Youling, Xing often followed him, was specially rewarded, and rose in successive promotions to commander of the Heavenly Martial.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned in Hedong and visited Youling, Xing often accompanied him, received special rewards, and rose to commander of the Heavenly Martial.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，改御前忠佐步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: During Duangong he was changed to deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Foot before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During Duangong he was made deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Foot before the throne.

sentences.zh: 王超為並、代部署，奏興隨軍，遣戍汾州。

translations.literal: When Wang Chao was commander of Bing and Dai, he memorialized that Xing should follow the army and sent him to garrison Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chao was commander of Bing and Dai, he memorialized that Xing should follow the army and sent him to garrison Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，李繼隆行營河西，興隸麾下，部清朔、龍衛諸軍，克綏、夏、銀州，繼隆命權知夏州。

translations.literal: The next year Li Jilong's field headquarters went west of the river; Xing was placed under his command, directed the Qing and Long guards and other armies, captured Sui, Xia, and Yin prefectures, and Jilong ordered him acting prefect of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Jilong's field headquarters went west of the river. Xing served under him, directed the Qing and Long guards and other armies, captured Sui, Xia, and Yin prefectures, and Jilong appointed him acting prefect of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 尋還屯所，受詔提轄河東緣邊城池、器甲、芻糧。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his garrison post and received an edict to take overall charge of the frontier cities, weapons and armor, and fodder of eastern Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to his garrison and received an edict placing him in overall charge of the frontier cities, weapons, armor, and fodder of eastern Hedong.

sentences.zh: 至道初，繼隆薦其材幹，召補禦龍弩直都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, Jilong recommended his ability and he was recalled to fill the post of adjutant of the Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhidao, Jilong recommended his ability and he was recalled as adjutant of the Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，為馬軍都軍頭、領蒙州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made chief commander of the Horse and nominal prefect of Mengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was made chief commander of the Horse and nominal prefect of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，真授憲州刺史、知霸州，徙滄州副都部署，移石、隰駐泊。

translations.literal: In the third year he was formally appointed prefect of Xianzhou and made prefect of Bazhou, was transferred to deputy commander of Cangzhou, and moved to garrison at Shi and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was formally appointed prefect of Xianzhou and made prefect of Bazhou, transferred to deputy commander of Cangzhou, and moved to garrison at Shi and Xi.

sentences.zh: 會城綏州，詔與錢若水往視利害，事具《若水傳》。

translations.literal: When Suizhou was being fortified, an edict ordered him and Qian Ruoshui to go inspect the advantages and disadvantages; the matter is given in full in the Ruoshui biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Suizhou was being fortified, an edict ordered him and Qian Ruoshui to inspect the advantages and disadvantages. The matter is given in full in the biography of Qian Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 又徙涇原儀渭鎮戎軍部署。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to commander of the Jingyuan, Yi, Wei, and Zhenrong army.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to commander of the Jingyuan, Yi, Wei, and Zhenrong army.

sentences.zh: 上言鎮戎軍去渭州瓦亭砦七十餘里，中有二堡，請留兵三百人戍之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Zhenrong army was more than seventy li from Wating fort of Weizhou and that between them were two forts, requesting that three hundred troops be left to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Zhenrong army lay more than seventy li from Wating fort of Weizhou, with two forts between, and requested that three hundred troops be left to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 俄與曹瑋、秦翰領兵抵鎮戎軍西北武延鹹泊川，掩擊蕃寇章埋族帳，斬二百餘級，生擒三百餘人，奪鎧甲、牛羊、駝馬三萬計。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Cao Wei and Qin Han, he led troops to Wuyan Salt Marsh on the northwest of Zhenrong army and made a surprise attack on the Fan bandit Zhangmai clan camps, beheading more than two hundred, capturing more than three hundred alive, and seizing on the order of thirty thousand sets of armor, cattle, sheep, and camels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, together with Cao Wei and Qin Han, he led troops to Wuyan Salt Marsh northwest of Zhenrong army and made a surprise attack on the Zhangmai clan camps, beheading more than two hundred, capturing more than three hundred alive, and seizing on the order of thirty thousand sets of armor, cattle, sheep, and camels.

sentences.zh: 詔書嘉獎，賜金帶、錦袍、器幣。

translations.literal: An edict praised and rewarded him and granted a gold belt, brocade robe, and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised and rewarded him and granted a gold belt, brocade robe, and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 繼遷所部康奴族，往歲鈔劫靈州援糧，恃險與眾，尤桀黠難制。

translations.literal: The Kangnu clan under Jiqian's command, which in past years had raided the grain sent to relieve Lingzhou, relied on difficult terrain and numbers and were especially crafty and hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangnu clan under Jiqian's command had in past years raided grain sent to relieve Lingzhou. Relying on difficult terrain and superior numbers, they were especially crafty and hard to control.

sentences.zh: 復與秦翰等合眾進討，窮其巢穴，俘老幼、獲器畜甚眾，盡焚掘其窖藏。

translations.literal: Again, together with Qin Han and others, he combined forces for a forward attack, reached their nest lairs, captured many old and young and seized livestock in great numbers, and burned and dug up all their stored caches.
translations.idiomatic: Again, together with Qin Han and others, he combined forces, advanced to their nest lairs, captured many old and young and seized livestock in great numbers, and burned and dug up all their stored caches.

sentences.zh: 復詔褒之，仍加賜賚。

translations.literal: Again an edict praised him and additionally granted gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Again an edict praised him and granted additional gifts.

sentences.zh: 其年，六穀大首領潘羅支言，欲率諸蕃擊賊，請會兵靈州。

translations.literal: That year the great chieftain of the Liugu, Pan Luozhi, said he wished to lead the various Fan to attack the bandits and requested to assemble troops at Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year the great chieftain of the Liugu, Pan Luozhi, said he wished to lead the various Fan to attack the rebels and requested to assemble troops at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以道遠難刻師期，詔興侯羅支報至，即勒所部過天都山以援，勿須奏命。

translations.literal: The emperor, on the ground that the road was distant and it was hard to fix a date for the army, issued an edict Xing to wait until Luozhi's report arrived, then immediately lead his command past Tiandu Mountain to relieve them without needing to memorialize for approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the road was distant and it was hard to fix a date for the army. He issued an edict Xing to wait until Luozhi's report arrived, then immediately lead his command past Tiandu Mountain to relieve them without needing to memorialize for approval.

sentences.zh: 會繼遷死，事寢。

translations.literal: When Jiqian died the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian died the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，遷本州團練使、知徐州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he was transferred to regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and made prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde he was transferred to regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and made prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 興起行伍，有武略，所至頗著聲績。

translations.literal: Xing rose from the ranks, had military stratagem, and wherever he served achieved considerable reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Xing rose from the ranks, had military stratagem, and wherever he served achieved considerable reputation and success.

sentences.zh: 真宗言軍校之材，必以興為能。

translations.literal: Zhenzong said that among military officers' talents, Xing must be counted able.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said that among military officers' talents, Xing must be counted able.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，召為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、領登州防禦使，出為邠寧環慶路副都部署兼知邠州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled as commander of all four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defender of Dengzhou, and sent out as deputy commander of the Binning and Huanqing circuit and acting prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled as commander of all four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defender of Dengzhou, then sent out as deputy commander of the Binning and Huanqing circuit and acting prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐擅釋劫盜，罷軍職，改敘州防禦使、知懷州。

translations.literal: For releasing robbers on his own authority he was punished by removal from military office and changed to defender of Xuzhou and prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For releasing robbers on his own authority he was removed from military office and made defender of Xuzhou and prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 許均，開封人。

translations.literal: Xu Jun was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jun was a native of Kaifeng.
