sentences.zh: 父邈，太常博士。

translations.literal: His father Miao was a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao was a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 均，建隆中應募為龍捷卒，征遼州，以功補武騎十將，賜錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: Jun, during the Jianlong era, answered the recruitment call as a soldier of the Dragon Swift, campaigned against Liaozhou, and for merit was appointed deputy commander of ten of the Martial Cavalry and granted a brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianlong era Jun enlisted in the Dragon Swift, campaigned against Liaozhou, and for merit was appointed deputy commander of ten of the Martial Cavalry and granted a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，遷武騎副兵馬使。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era he was transferred to deputy horse-and-troop commander of the Martial Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he was transferred to deputy horse-and-troop commander of the Martial Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從曹彬征金陵，率眾陷水砦，流矢貫手。

translations.literal: He followed Cao Bin in the campaign against Jinling, led troops in the assault on the water fort, and a stray arrow pierced his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cao Bin in the campaign against Jinling, led troops in the assault on the water fort, and a stray arrow pierced his hand.

sentences.zh: 改本軍使。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of his original army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of his original army.

sentences.zh: 從征河東，攻隆州城，先登，陷之，中八創。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign in Hedong, attacked Longzhou city, was first to ascend, took it, and received eight wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign in Hedong, was first to scale Longzhou city and take it, and was wounded eight times.

sentences.zh: 遷副指揮使，前後屢被賞賚。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander and was repeatedly rewarded before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander and was repeatedly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 出屯杭州，妖僧紹倫結黨為亂，均從巡檢使周瑩悉擒殺之。

translations.literal: He was sent to garrison Hangzhou; the sorcerer-monk Shaolun formed a faction and made rebellion, and Jun, following the inspection commissioner Zhou Ying, captured and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to garrison Hangzhou, he followed inspection commissioner Zhou Ying in capturing and killing the sorcerer-monk Shaolun and his rebel faction.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，補指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed commander.

sentences.zh: 從李繼隆、秦翰赴夏州。

translations.literal: He followed Li Jilong and Qin Han to Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Jilong and Qin Han to Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 擒趙保忠，令均率兵衛守。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong was captured, Jun was ordered to lead troops to guard and hold him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong was captured, Jun was ordered to lead troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 改龍衛第四指揮使，俄屯夏州，賊來犯境，一日十二戰，走之。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of the Fourth Company of the Dragon Guard; soon he garrisoned Xiazhou, and when bandits came to invade the border he fought twelve battles in a single day and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Fourth Company of the Dragon Guard and soon garrisoned Xiazhou. When rebels invaded the border he fought twelve battles in one day and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 又從石普擊賊於原州牛欄砦，深入，獲牛羊、漢生口甚眾。

translations.literal: He again followed Shi Pu in striking bandits at Niulan fort in Yuanzhou, penetrated deep, and seized cattle, sheep, and Han captives in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Shi Pu in attacking rebels at Niulan fort in Yuanzhou, pushed deep into enemy territory, and seized large numbers of cattle, sheep, and Han captives.

sentences.zh: 普表上其功，遷第三軍指揮使。

translations.literal: Pu memorialized his merit and he was transferred to commander of the Third Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu memorialized his achievements and he was transferred to commander of the Third Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，以御前忠佐馬軍都軍頭戍秦州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne and garrisoned Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was made chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne and garrisoned Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 王均之亂，遣乘傳之蜀，隸雷有終麾下，守魚橋門，又從秦翰追殺賊黨於廣都，降其眾七千餘。

translations.literal: During Wang Jun's rebellion he was sent by relay post to Shu, was placed under Lei Youzhong, guarded Yuqiao Gate, and again followed Qin Han in pursuing and killing rebel bands at Guangdu, accepting the surrender of more than seven thousand of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Jun's rebellion he was sent by relay to Shu, served under Lei Youzhong, guarded Yuqiao Gate, and followed Qin Han in pursuing rebels at Guangdu, accepting the surrender of more than seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 驛召授東西班都虞候、領順州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned by relay post and appointed adjutant of the Eastern and Western Companies and nominal prefect of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned by imperial relay, he was appointed adjutant of the Eastern and Western Companies and nominal prefect of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，稍遷散員都虞候。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was gradually transferred to adjutant of the Unattached.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was gradually promoted to adjutant of the Unattached.

sentences.zh: 嘗召見，訪以北面邊事，翌日，真拜磁州刺史、深州兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was once summoned for audience and questioned about northern frontier affairs; the next day he was formally appointed prefect of Cizhou and superintendent of the horse and foot of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for audience and questioned about northern frontier affairs. The next day he was formally appointed prefect of Cizhou and superintendent of the horse and foot of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，改涇州駐泊部署。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to garrison commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made garrison commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，知鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: After several months he was made prefect of Zhenrong army.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was made commander of Zhenrong army.

sentences.zh: 嘗出巡警，至隴山木峽口，真宗以其無故離城，慮有狂寇奔突，詔書戒敕。

translations.literal: He once went out on patrol as far as Muxia Pass of Long Mountain; Zhenzong, because he had left the city without cause, feared that wild bandits might make a sudden raid, and issued an edict a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He once went on patrol as far as Muxia Pass on Long Mountain. Emperor Zhenzong, fearing a sudden raid because he had left the city without cause, issued an edict of warning.

sentences.zh: 俄以其不明吏治，用曹瑋代之，徙為邠州駐泊部署，改永興軍部署。

translations.literal: Soon, because he was not clear in civil administration, Cao Wei was used to replace him; he was transferred to garrison commander of Binzhou and changed to commander of the Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because he was incompetent in civil administration, Cao Wei replaced him. He was transferred to garrison commander of Binzhou and then commander of the Yongxing army.

sentences.zh: 車駕將巡澶淵，詔均與知府向敏中及鳳翔梁鼎同提總諸州巡檢捕盜事，至河陽，召赴行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to tour Chanyuan, an edict ordered Jun, together with the prefect Xiang Minzhong and Liang Ding of Fengxiang, jointly to take overall charge of the inspection and capture of bandits in the various prefectures; when they reached Heyang he was summoned to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to tour Chanyuan, Jun was ordered together with prefect Xiang Minzhong and Liang Ding of Fengxiang to take overall charge of bandit suppression in the various prefectures. At Heyang he was summoned to the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 時有王長壽者，本亡命卒，有勇力，多計慮，聚徒百餘。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Wang Changshou, originally a fugitive soldier, brave and strong, full of schemes, who gathered more than a hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a Wang Changshou, originally a fugitive soldier, brave and resourceful, who gathered more than a hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 是春，抵陳留剽劫，縣民捕之不獲，朝廷遣使益兵，逐之澶、濮間。

translations.literal: That spring he reached Chenliu to plunder and rob; the county people could not capture him, and the court sent envoys to add troops and pursued him between Chun and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: That spring he raided Chenliu. Local forces could not capture him, and the court sent envoys to reinforce the pursuit between Chun and Pu.

sentences.zh: 會契丹南侵，夾河民庶驚擾，長壽結黨愈眾，人皆患之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded south, the people on both banks of the river were alarmed and disturbed; Changshou's faction grew ever larger and everyone regarded him as a plague.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded south, the people along the river were thrown into alarm. Changshou's band grew larger and became a widespread menace.

sentences.zh: 均至胙城，長壽與其徒五千餘人入縣鈔掠，均部下徒兵裼袒與鬥。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Zuocheng, Changshou with more than five thousand of his followers entered the county to plunder; Jun's soldiers, bared to the waist, fought them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Zuocheng, Changshou entered the county with more than five thousand men to plunder. Jun's troops, fighting bare to the waist, engaged them.

sentences.zh: 均以方略誘之，生擒長壽，斬獲惡黨皆盡。

translations.literal: Jun by stratagem lured them, captured Changshou alive, and beheaded and seized the wicked faction to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lured them by stratagem, captured Changshou alive, and killed or captured his entire band.

sentences.zh: 上以方禦敵，未欲因捕賊獎均。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was then facing the enemy, did not wish to reward Jun for capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, then facing the Khitan enemy, did not wish to reward Jun yet for capturing bandits.

sentences.zh: 但賞均部下卒，被傷者賜帛遷級焉。

translations.literal: He only rewarded Jun's soldiers; those wounded were granted silk and promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded only Jun's soldiers; the wounded received silk and promotions in rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，追敘前勞，擢為本州團練使，尋出知代州。

translations.literal: The next year, recounting his earlier merit, he was promoted to regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and soon sent out as prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, recounting his earlier merit, he was promoted to regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and soon posted as prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，均被疾，以米銳代還，未至而均卒。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year Jun fell ill; Mi Rui was sent to replace him and return, but before Rui arrived Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year Jun fell ill. Mi Rui was sent to replace him, but Jun died before Rui arrived.

sentences.zh: 錄其子懷忠為奉禮郎，懷信為侍禁。

translations.literal: His son Huaizhong was enrolled as ceremonial attendant and Huaixin as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaizhong was enrolled as ceremonial attendant and Huaixin as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 幼子懷德，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger son Huaide has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Huaide has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張進，兗州曲阜人，拳勇善射，挽強及石餘。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin was a man of Qufu in Yanzhou, skilled in boxing and brave in archery, able to draw a strong bow of more than a stone in weight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin was a native of Qufu in Yanzhou. He was skilled in boxing and archery and could draw a bow of more than a stone in weight.

sentences.zh: 應募曹州，隸鎮兵。

translations.literal: He answered the recruitment call in Caozhou and was assigned to the garrison army.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in Caozhou and was assigned to the garrison army.

sentences.zh: 太祖親選勇士，奇進才力，以補控鶴官，積勞至禦龍弩直都虞候、領恩州刺史。

translations.literal: Taizu personally selected brave warriors, marveled at Jin's talent and strength, appointed him to the Crane Control office, and through accumulated merit he rose to adjutant of the Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct and nominal prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu personally selected brave warriors, admired Jin's strength and ability, appointed him to the Crane Control office, and through accumulated merit rose to adjutant of the Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct and nominal prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道中，兼御前忠佐步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: During the Zhidao era he was additionally chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Foot before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era he was additionally chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Foot before the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗幸內廄，進以親校執鉞前導，體質魁岸，迥出儕輩。

translations.literal: Taizong once visited the inner stables; Jin, as his personal officer, bore the axe and led the way before him; his physique was towering and far surpassed his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once visited the inner stables. Jin, as his personal officer, bore the ceremonial axe and led the way. His towering physique far surpassed his peers.

sentences.zh: 太宗熟視異之，擢為天武右廂都指揮使、領賀州團練使。

translations.literal: Taizong looked at him closely with wonder and promoted him to commander of the Right Wing of the Heavenly Martial and regimental commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong looked at him with close attention and wonder, then promoted him to commander of the Right Wing of the Heavenly Martial and regimental commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遷昭州防禦使，充龍神衛四廂都指揮使、京城左右廂巡檢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was transferred to defender of Zhaozhou, made commander of all four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and inspector of the left and right wings of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was made defender of Zhaozhou, commander of all four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and inspector of the left and right wings of the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷捧日、天武四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to commander of all four wings of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to commander of all four wings of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，閱武近郊，進與殿前都指揮使王超親執金鼓，節其進退，軍容甚肅。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year, when troops were reviewed in the suburbs, Jin and Wang Chao, commander of the Palace Front, personally beat the gold drums and regulated advance and retreat; the army's bearing was very stern.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year, during a suburban military review, Jin and Wang Chao, commander of the Palace Front, personally beat the gold drums and regulated advance and retreat. The army's bearing was exceptionally stern.

sentences.zh: 從上北征，又與超管勾大陣及先鋒策應。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the northern expedition and again, with Chao, managed the great formation and the vanguard assault corps.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the northern expedition and again, with Chao, managed the main formation and the vanguard assault corps.

sentences.zh: 三年，權殿前都虞候，遷侍衛步軍都虞候、鎮州副部署，徙天雄軍部署。

translations.literal: In the third year he was acting chief adjutant of the Palace Front, transferred to adjutant of the Imperial Foot and deputy commander of Zhenzhou, and moved to commander of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was acting chief adjutant of the Palace Front, made adjutant of the Imperial Foot and deputy commander of Zhenzhou, then commander of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 會河決鄆州王陵口，發數州丁男塞之，命進董其役，凡月餘畢，詔褒之。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke through at Wangling Pass in Yanzhou, corvée laborers from several prefectures were mobilized to block it; Jin was ordered to supervise the work, which was completed in just over a month, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke through at Wangling Pass in Yanzhou, corvée labor from several prefectures was mobilized to block it. Jin supervised the work, which was finished in just over a month, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 移並、代副都部署。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy commander of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 李重貴

translations.literal: Li Zhonggui
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhonggui

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，契丹南侵，議屯兵楊疃，張凝領先鋒遇敵，重貴率策應兵酣戰，全軍而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, when the Khitan invaded south, it was debated to encamp troops at Yangtuan; Zhang Ning led the vanguard and met the enemy, and Zhonggui led the assault-support troops in fierce battle and returned with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping, when the Khitan invaded south, the court debated encamping at Yangtuan. Zhang Ning's vanguard met the enemy and Zhonggui led the assault-support troops in fierce fighting, returning with his force intact.

sentences.zh: 范廷召自定州至，遇契丹兵交戰，康保裔大陣為敵所覆，重貴與凝赴援，腹背受敵，自申至寅，疾力戰，敵乃退。

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao came from Dingzhou and met the Khitan in battle; Kang Baoyin's great formation was overrun by the enemy; Zhonggui and Ning went to their relief, were attacked front and rear, and from the hour shen to the hour yin fought with desperate force until the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao came from Dingzhou and engaged the Khitan. Kang Baoyin's main formation was overrun. Zhonggui and Ning rushed to the rescue, were attacked front and rear, and from mid-afternoon until dawn fought with desperate force until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時諸將頗失部分，獨重貴與凝全軍還屯。

translations.literal: At the time the various generals largely lost good order; only Zhonggui and Ning returned with their whole armies to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Most generals had lost good order. Only Zhonggui and Ning returned with their whole armies intact.

sentences.zh: 凝議上將士功狀，重貴喟然曰：“大將陷沒而吾曹計功，何面目也！

translations.literal: Ning proposed to memorialize the merits of officers and soldiers; Zhonggui sighed and said: "The great commander has perished and we would calculate merit — what face have we!
translations.idiomatic: Ning proposed to memorialize the troops' merits. Zhonggui sighed and said, "Our great commander has fallen and we would count merit for ourselves — what face have we left?

sentences.zh: ”上聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: " When the emperor heard of this he praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard this he praised him.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以勞進階及食邑，徙知貝州，召至勞問，復遣入郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year, for his merit he was advanced in rank and fief, transferred to prefect of Beizhou, summoned to court for consolation, and again sent into the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, for his merit he was advanced in rank and fief, made prefect of Beizhou, summoned to court for consolation, and again sent to his post.

sentences.zh: 是冬，徙滄州駐泊副都部署兼知州事。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to deputy garrison commander of Cangzhou and acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was transferred to deputy garrison commander of Cangzhou and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 以疾求還京就醫藥，既愈，連為邢州、天雄軍二部署，又知冀州。

translations.literal: He begged to return to the capital for medical treatment because of illness; after he recovered he served in succession as commander of Xingzhou and the Tianxiong army and again as prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to return to the capital for medical treatment. After he recovered he served in succession as commander of Xingzhou, the Tianxiong army, and prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，車駕幸澶淵，召還，為大內都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, when the imperial carriage went to Chanyuan, he was recalled and made overall commander of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, when the emperor went to Chanyuan, he was recalled and made overall commander of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 明年春，出知鄭州，以疾甚，授左武衛大將軍、領潘州防禦使，改左羽林軍大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year he was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou; because his illness was severe he was appointed great general of the Left Martial Guard and defender of Panzhou, then changed to great general of the Left Feathered Forest and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was posted as prefect of Zhengzhou. Because his illness was severe he was appointed great general of the Left Martial Guard and defender of Panzhou, then retired as great general of the Left Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.

sentences.zh: 呼延贊

translations.literal: Hu Yanzan
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yanzan

sentences.zh: 呼延贊，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Hu Yanzan was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yanzan was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父琮，周淄州馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Cong was horse-and-foot commander of Zizhou under the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cong had been horse-and-foot commander of Zizhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 贊少為驍騎卒，太祖以其材勇，補東班長，入承旨，遷驍雄軍使。

translations.literal: In youth Zan was a soldier of the Valiant Cavalry; Taizu, for his talent and courage, appointed him squad leader of the Eastern Class, entered the Imperial Secretariat, and transferred him to commander of the Valiant Hero army.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zan served in the Valiant Cavalry. Taizu, impressed by his talent and courage, appointed him squad leader of the Eastern Class, brought him into the Imperial Secretariat, and made him commander of the Valiant Hero army.

sentences.zh: 從王全斌討西川，身當前鋒，中數創，以功補副指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Quanbin in the campaign against western Shu, took the front himself, received several wounds, and for merit was appointed deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Quanbin against western Shu, fought at the front, was wounded several times, and for merit was appointed deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，太宗親選軍校，以贊為鐵騎軍指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, Taizong personally selected military officers and made Zan commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, Taizong personally selected military officers and made Zan commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，先登乘城，及堞而墜者數四，面賜金帛獎之。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan he was first to ascend and scale the wall; he fell from the parapet several times, and the emperor face-to-face granted him gold and silks in reward.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Taiyuan he was first to scale the wall, fell from the parapet several times, and was rewarded face-to-face with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 七年，從崔翰戍定州，翰言其勇，擢為馬軍副都軍頭，稍遷內員寮直都虞候。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Cui Han to garrison Dingzhou; Han spoke of his courage and he was promoted to deputy chief commander of the Horse, and gradually transferred to adjutant of the Inner Attendant Direct.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Cui Han to garrison Dingzhou. Han praised his courage and he was promoted to deputy chief commander of the Horse, then gradually to adjutant of the Inner Attendant Direct.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，加馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was made deputy chief commander of the horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was made deputy chief commander of the horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻陣圖、兵要及樹營砦之策，求領邊任。

translations.literal: He once presented battle formations, military essentials, and plans for building camps and forts, and requested a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented battle formations, military essentials, and plans for building camps and forts, and requested a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 召見，令之作武藝。

translations.literal: When summoned for audience he was ordered to perform martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience he was ordered to perform martial arts.

sentences.zh: 贊具裝執馳騎，揮鐵鞭、棗槊，旋繞廷中數四，又引其四子必興、必改、必求、必顯以入，迭舞劍盤槊。

translations.literal: Zan, in full armor, mounted and spurred his horse, wielded an iron whip and jujube spear, wheeled several times around the hall, and also brought in his four sons Bixing, Bigai, Biqiu, and Bixian to enter, each in turn dancing with sword and circling spear.
translations.idiomatic: Zan appeared in full armor, mounted his horse, wielded an iron whip and jujube spear, and wheeled several times around the hall. He then brought in his four sons Bixing, Bigai, Biqiu, and Bixian, who danced in turn with sword and circling spear.

sentences.zh: 賜白金數百兩及四子衣帶。

translations.literal: He was granted several hundred taels of white gold and robes and belts for his four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted several hundred taels of white gold and robes and belts for his four sons.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，領富州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he held nominal prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he held nominal prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄與輔超並加都軍頭。

translations.literal: Soon he and Fu Chao were together made chief commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Fu Chao were together made chief commanders.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，出為保州刺史、冀州副都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was sent out as prefect of Baozhou and deputy commander of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he was posted as prefect of Baozhou and deputy commander of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 至屯所，以無統御材，改遼州刺史。

translations.literal: When he reached his garrison, because he lacked talent for overall command he was changed to prefect of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his garrison, because he lacked talent for overall command, he was transferred to prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又以不能治民，復為都軍頭、領扶州刺史，加康州團練使。

translations.literal: Again, because he could not govern the people, he was restored as chief commander with nominal prefect of Fuzhou and additionally made regimental commissioner of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because he could not govern the people well, he was restored as chief commander with nominal prefect of Fuzhou and additionally made regimental commissioner of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，從幸大名，為行宮內外都巡檢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he followed the emperor to Daming and was made overall inspector inside and outside the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he followed the emperor to Daming and was made overall inspector inside and outside the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗補軍校，皆敘己功，或至喧嘩，贊獨進曰：“臣月奉百千，所用不及半，忝幸多矣。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong once filled military officer posts, all recounted their own merit, and some even clamored noisily; Zan alone advanced and said: "Your servant's monthly salary is a hundred thousand, and I use less than half; I am already excessively favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong once filled military posts, the others all recounted their own merit, some even clamoring noisily. Zan alone stepped forward and said, "Your servant receives a hundred thousand in monthly salary and uses less than half. I am already excessively favored.

sentences.zh: 自念無以報國，不敢更求遷擢，將恐福過災生。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I have no means to repay the state, I dare not seek further promotion, lest fortune pass its measure and disaster be born.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that I have no means to repay the state, I dare not seek further promotion, lest good fortune exceed its measure and disaster follow.

sentences.zh: ”再拜而退，眾嘉其知分。

translations.literal: " He bowed twice and withdrew, and the crowd praised his knowing his measure.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed twice and withdrew, and the assembly praised his knowing his measure.

sentences.zh: 三年，元德皇太后園陵，命掌護儀衛，及還而卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, for the park tomb of the Yuande Empress Dowager, he was ordered to take charge of ceremonial guards, and on his return he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to take charge of ceremonial guards for the park tomb of the Yuande Empress Dowager and died on his return.

sentences.zh: 贊有膽勇，鷙悍輕率，常言願死於敵。

translations.literal: Zan had courage and daring, was fierce, overbearing, and rash, and often said he wished to die fighting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was courageous, fierce, overbearing, and rash, and often said he wished to die fighting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遍文其體為“赤心殺賊”字，至於妻孥僕使皆然，諸子耳後別刺字曰：“出門忘家為國，臨陣忘死為主。

translations.literal: He inscribed his whole body with the characters "Loyal Heart, Slayer of Bandits," and even his wife, children, and servants were the same; on his sons' ears he separately tattooed: "Leaving home, forget family for the state; entering battle, forget death for the lord."
translations.idiomatic: He tattooed his whole body with the words "Loyal Heart, Slayer of Bandits," and even his wife, children, and servants did the same. Behind his sons' ears he tattooed separately: "Leaving home, forget family for the state; entering battle, forget death for the lord."

sentences.zh: ”及作破陣刀、降魔杵，鐵折上巾，兩旁有刃，皆重十數斤。

translations.literal: He also made a battle-breaking saber, a demon-subduing staff, and an iron folded-head turban with blades on both sides, each weighing more than ten pounds.
translations.idiomatic: He also made a battle-breaking saber, a demon-subduing staff, and an iron folded-head turban with blades on both sides, each weighing more than ten pounds.

sentences.zh: 絳帕首，乘騅馬，服飾詭異。

translations.literal: With a crimson headcloth he rode a piebald horse; his dress was bizarre.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a crimson headcloth, rode a piebald horse, and dressed in bizarre fashion.

sentences.zh: 性復鄙誕不近理，盛冬以水沃孩幼，冀其長能寒而勁健。

translations.literal: His nature was again vulgar and absurd, not close to reason; in deep winter he poured water over infants, hoping that when they grew up they would be able to endure cold and be strong and hardy.
translations.idiomatic: He was vulgar and absurd by nature. In deep winter he poured water over infants, hoping they would grow hardy enough to endure cold.

sentences.zh: 其子嘗病，贊刲股為羹療之。

translations.literal: When his son was ill, Zan cut flesh from his thigh to make broth to cure him.
translations.idiomatic: When his son fell ill, Zan cut flesh from his thigh to make a medicinal broth.

sentences.zh: 贊卒後，擢必顯為軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: After Zan's death, Bixian was promoted to deputy chief commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zan's death, Bixian was promoted to deputy chief commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加本州團練使、并州副都部署。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Yong was additionally made regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and deputy commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Liu Yong was additionally made regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and deputy commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，徙貝州，俄知瀛州，復為高陽關副都部署。

translations.literal: During Xianping he was transferred to Beizhou, soon made prefect of Yingzhou, and again made deputy commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he was transferred to Beizhou, soon made prefect of Yingzhou, and again deputy commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 時烽堠數警，用建議益邊兵，俟其南牧，即率驍銳出東路以牽制其勢，因圖上地形。

translations.literal: At the time the beacon towers were repeatedly alarmed; Yong proposed increasing frontier troops so that when the Khitan came south to pasture they could lead crack troops out on the eastern route to check the enemy's momentum, and he therefore submitted a map of the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The beacon towers were repeatedly alarmed. Yong proposed increasing frontier troops so that when the Khitan came south to pasture, crack troops could strike out on the eastern route to check their momentum, and he submitted a terrain map.

sentences.zh: 上召宰相閱視，可其奏，且令轉運使於保州、威虜、靜戎、順安軍預備資糧。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to review it, approved his memorial, and ordered the transport commissioners to prepare provisions in advance at Baozhou, Weilu, Jingrong, and Shun'an armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to review it, approved his plan, and ordered transport commissioners to prepare provisions in advance at Baozhou, Weilu, Jingrong, and Shun'an.

sentences.zh: 六年，命將三路出師扞敵，詔用與劉漢凝、田思明領兵五千，由東路會石普、孫全照掎角攻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to lead three routes out to resist the enemy; an edict ordered Yong, together with Liu Hanning and Tian Siming, to lead five thousand troops by the eastern route to join Shi Pu and Sun Quanzhao in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year three routes were ordered out against the enemy. Yong, Liu Hanning, and Tian Siming were issued an edict to lead five thousand troops by the eastern route to join Shi Pu and Sun Quanzhao in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 未幾，換鎮州副部署。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to deputy commander of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to deputy commander of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，為邢州部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was commander of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he was commander of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕北征，用以城守之勞，進爵邑，歷知齊、陳、潞三州，大中祥符二年卒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went on the northern expedition, for his merit in defending the cities he was advanced in noble rank and fief, served in succession as prefect of Qi, Chen, and Lu, and died in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition his merit in city defense won advancement in noble rank and fief. He served in succession as prefect of Qi, Chen, and Lu, and died in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 耿全斌

translations.literal: Geng Quanbin
translations.idiomatic: Geng Quanbin

sentences.zh: 從征太原，還，遇契丹於蒲陰，追擊至徐河，因據水口要害。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan, on the return he met the Khitan at Puyin, pursued them to the Xu River, and thereby held the key point at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from the Taiyuan campaign he met the Khitan at Puyin, pursued them to the Xu River, and seized the key point at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 遷補日騎副兵馬使、雲騎軍使，屯瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed deputy horse-and-troop commander of the Day-Riding and commander of the Cloud Cavalry, and garrisoned Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy horse-and-troop commander of the Day-Riding and commander of the Cloud Cavalry, and garrisoned Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 與契丹戰，所乘馬兩中流矢死，凡三易乘，戰不卻，契丹為引去。

translations.literal: In battle with the Khitan, the horses he rode were twice struck by arrows and killed; he changed mounts three times in all, did not retreat in battle, and the Khitan withdrew on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the Khitan, two of his horses were killed by arrows. He changed mounts three times, never retreated, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，擊蕃部於宥州，敗之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he struck Fan tribes at Youzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he attacked Fan tribes at Youzhou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 曆雲騎指揮使、御前忠佐馬軍副都軍頭，改馬軍都軍頭，戍深州，累轉散直都虞候、領順州刺史，改殿前左班都虞候、馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: He served successively as commander of the Cloud Cavalry and deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne, was changed to chief commander of the Horse, garrisoned Shenzhou, and through successive transfers became adjutant of the Unattached and nominal prefect of Shunzhou, then adjutant of the Left Company of the Palace Front and chief commander of the horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through commander of the Cloud Cavalry and deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse, became chief commander of the Horse, garrisoned Shenzhou, and through successive posts reached adjutant of the Unattached and nominal prefect of Shunzhou, then adjutant of the Left Company of the Palace Front and chief commander of the horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 全斌在軍中有能名。

translations.literal: Quanbin had a reputation for ability in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin enjoyed a reputation for ability in the army.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗召問邊事，全斌口陳利害，甚稱旨。

translations.literal: Zhenzong once summoned him to question him on frontier affairs; Quanbin stated advantages and disadvantages orally and greatly matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong once summoned him to question him on frontier affairs. Quanbin stated the advantages and disadvantages orally and greatly pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 因謂輔臣曰：“元澄、鄭誠、耿全斌，人多稱之。

translations.literal: He therefore said to the assisting ministers: "Yuan Cheng, Zheng Cheng, and Geng Quanbin — many people praise them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told the assisting ministers, "Yuan Cheng, Zheng Cheng, and Geng Quanbin are widely praised.

sentences.zh: 觀其詞氣，若有志操，止在宿衛，無以見其才，宜以邊郡試之。

translations.literal: Judging from their words and bearing, they seem to have will and integrity; kept only in palace guard service, there is no way to see their talent — they should be tried in frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from their words and bearing they seem men of will and integrity. Kept only in palace guard service, their talent cannot be seen. They should be tried on the frontier.

sentences.zh: ”遂拜雄州刺史、知深州，徙石、隰部署以備河西。

translations.literal: " He was therefore appointed prefect of Xiongzhou and made prefect of Shenzhou, and transferred to the Shi and Xi garrison command to guard the Hexi frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore appointed prefect of Xiongzhou and acting prefect of Shenzhou, then transferred to the Shi and Xi garrison command to guard the Hexi frontier.

sentences.zh: 繼遷死，全斌率兵入伏落關，誘蕃部來歸者數千人。

translations.literal: When Jiqian died, Quanbin led troops into Fuluo Pass and induced several thousand Fan tribes to come over.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian died, Quanbin led troops into Fuluo Pass and induced several thousand Fan tribes to submit.

sentences.zh: 俄知安肅軍，嘗繪山川險易為圖以獻。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Ansou army and once drew a map of mountains and rivers with their difficulties and eases to present.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of Ansou army and once drew and presented a map of the terrain's difficulties and advantages.

sentences.zh: 契丹來侵，自山北抵河滸，全斌遣子從政焚橋砦，分率精兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, coming from north of the mountains to the river bank, Quanbin sent his son Congzheng to burn bridges and forts and separately led crack troops to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded from north of the mountains to the river bank, Quanbin sent his son Congzheng to burn bridges and forts and led elite troops in a separate attack that drove them off.

sentences.zh: 改冀州刺史、高陽關鈐轄，擢從政為侍禁、寄班祗候。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Jizhou and superintendent of Gaoyang Pass, and Congzheng was promoted to palace attendant and acting relay attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jizhou and superintendent of Gaoyang Pass. His son Congzheng was promoted to palace attendant and acting relay attendant.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，封禪泰山，以為濮州鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, for the Feng and Chan rites at Mount Tai, he was made superintendent of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, for the Feng and Chan rites at Mount Tai, he was made superintendent of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年還京師，卒。

translations.literal: That year he returned to the capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he returned to the capital and died.

sentences.zh: 周仁美

translations.literal: Zhou Renmei
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Renmei

sentences.zh: 周仁美，深州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Renmei was a man of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Renmei was a native of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，應募隸貝州驍捷軍。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era he answered the recruitment call and was assigned to the Valiant Swift army of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he enlisted and was assigned to the Valiant Swift army of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 關南李漢超選備給使，屢捕獲契丹諜者。

translations.literal: Li Hankao of Guannan selected him as supply attendant and he repeatedly captured Khitan spies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hankao of Guannan selected him as supply attendant, and he repeatedly captured Khitan spies.

sentences.zh: 從漢超戰於西嘉山，身中重創，補隊長。

translations.literal: He followed Hankao in battle at Xijiashan, received grave wounds in the body, and was appointed squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hankao in battle at Xijiashan, was gravely wounded, and was appointed squad leader.

sentences.zh: 漢超上其功，隸殿前班，賜衣帶、鞍勒馬、什物、奴婢、器械。

translations.literal: Hankao memorialized his merit; he was assigned to the Palace Front company and granted robes, belts, saddled horses, goods, male and female servants, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Hankao memorialized his merit. He was assigned to the Palace Front company and granted robes, belts, saddled horses, goods, servants, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 命王繼恩引入縱觀，過祗候庫，太祖問其力能負錢幾許，仁美曰：“臣可勝七八萬。

translations.literal: Wang Jien was ordered to introduce him for a general viewing; passing the attendants' storehouse, Taizu asked how much cash his strength could bear, and Renmei said: "Your servant can bear seventy or eighty thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jien was ordered to introduce him for inspection. Passing the attendants' storehouse, Taizu asked how much cash he could carry on his back. Renmei said, "Your servant can bear seventy or eighty thousand."

sentences.zh: ”太祖曰：“可惜壓死。

translations.literal: " Taizu said: "It would be a pity to crush you to death."
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu said, "It would be a pity to crush you to death."

sentences.zh: ”止命負四萬五千，因賜之。

translations.literal: " He ordered him to bear only forty-five thousand and therefore granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him to bear only forty-five thousand and granted him that amount.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右班都知、御前忠佐馬軍副都軍頭，戍環州。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to commander of the Right Company and deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne, and garrisoned Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to commander of the Right Company and deputy chief commander of the Loyal Assistants Horse before the throne, and garrisoned Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時牛耶泥族累歲為寇，仁美與陳德玄、宋思恭往擊之，斬首三千級，獲牛羊三百餘，發戎族囷窖以餉師。

translations.literal: At the time the Niuyeni clan had raided year after year; Renmei, together with Chen Dexuan and Song Sigong, went to attack them, beheaded three thousand, seized more than three hundred cattle and sheep, and opened the Fan tribes' granaries and cellars to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Niuyeni clan had raided year after year. Renmei, Chen Dexuan, and Song Sigong attacked them, beheaded three thousand, seized more than three hundred cattle and sheep, and opened Fan granaries to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 又與思恭討募窟泉岌拖族，格鬥，斬八十餘級。

translations.literal: Again, with Sigong he attacked the Mukukuquan Jituo clan in close combat and beheaded more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Again, with Sigong he attacked the Mukukuquan Jituo clan in close combat and beheaded more than eighty.

sentences.zh: 至道初，石昌牛耶泥族復叛，德玄令仁美提兵撫輯之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao the Shichang Niuyeni clan rebelled again; Dexuan ordered Renmei to lead troops to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhidao the Shichang Niuyeni clan rebelled again. Dexuan ordered Renmei to lead troops to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 仁美謂石昌鎮主和文顯曰：“此賊不除，邊患未弭。

translations.literal: Renmei said to the fort commander of Shichang, Hewenxian: "If this bandit is not removed, the frontier trouble will not be stilled."
translations.idiomatic: Renmei told the Shichang fort commander Hewenxian, "If this bandit is not removed, the frontier will not be at peace."

sentences.zh: ”因厚設殽酒，召酋長二十八人縛送州獄，自是諸族懾畏。

translations.literal: " He therefore set out a lavish feast of food and wine, summoned twenty-eight chieftains, bound them, and sent them to the prefectural prison; from then on the various clans were awed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: " He set a lavish feast, summoned twenty-eight chieftains, bound them, and sent them to the prefectural prison. From then on the various clans were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 二年，又與馬紹忠、白守榮、田紹斌部芻糧趣清遠軍，仁美為先鋒。

translations.literal: In the second year, again with Ma Shaozhong, Bai Shourong, and Tian Shaobin he transported fodder in haste to Qingyuan army; Renmei was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he again joined Ma Shaozhong, Bai Shourong, and Tian Shaobin in rushing fodder to Qingyuan army as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至岐子平，與虜角，走之。

translations.literal: When they reached Qizi Plain they fought the barbarians at close quarters and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: At Qizi Plain they fought the enemy at close quarters and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 明日，又戰於浦洛河，自巳至戌，戰數十合，進壁乾河。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again on the Pulu River from the hour si to the hour xu, fought several dozen engagements, and advanced to fortify on the Dry River.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again on the Pulu River from mid-morning until evening in several dozen engagements, then advanced to fortify on the Dry River.

sentences.zh: 紹忠、守榮皆敗走，紹斌退止浦洛，獨仁美所部不滿三千，身中八創，護芻糧、官吏直抵清遠。

translations.literal: Shaozhong and Shourong both were defeated and fled; Shaobin retreated and halted at Pulu; Renmei alone commanded fewer than three thousand, received eight wounds in the body, and protected the fodder and officials straight through to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhong and Shourong were defeated and fled. Shaobin halted at Pulu. Renmei alone commanded fewer than three thousand men, was wounded eight times, and escorted the fodder and officials through to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 紹斌繼至，深歎其勇幹，表上其功。

translations.literal: When Shaobin arrived afterward he deeply sighed at his courage and ability and memorialized his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaobin arrived afterward he deeply admired Renmei's courage and ability and memorialized his merit.

sentences.zh: 時運糧民道路被傷者相繼，仁美領徒援護，悉抵環州。

translations.literal: At the time transport laborers on the roads were wounded in succession; Renmei led corvée troops to escort and protect them, and all reached Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transport workers were being wounded all along the roads. Renmei led corvée troops to escort them, and all reached Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遇虜於橐駝路，擊走之。

translations.literal: He again met the barbarians on Camel Road and struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He again met the enemy on Camel Road and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸蕃每貢馬京師，為繼遷邀擊，仁美領騎士為援，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever the various Fan presented horses at the capital they were intercepted by Jiqian; Renmei led horsemen as escort and the bandits did not dare violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever the various Fan presented horses at the capital Jiqian intercepted them. Renmei led cavalry as escort and the rebels did not dare interfere.

sentences.zh: 補澶州龍衛軍都虞候，部署李繼隆奏留麾下，選軍中伉健者千人，令仁美領之，屢入敵境，戰有功。

translations.literal: He was appointed adjutant of the Dragon Guard of Chunzhou; commander Li Jilong memorialized to keep him under his command, selected a thousand sturdy men from the army, and ordered Renmei to lead them; he repeatedly entered enemy territory and fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed adjutant of the Dragon Guard of Chunzhou. Li Jilong memorialized to retain him, selected a thousand sturdy soldiers, and ordered Renmei to lead them on repeated incursions with merit.

sentences.zh: 俄還澶州。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 召見，會令諸軍射，仁美自陳筋力未衰，願對殿廷發二矢，上許之。

translations.literal: When summoned for audience, it happened that the various armies were ordered to shoot; Renmei himself stated that his sinew strength had not declined and he wished to shoot two arrows in the court hall, and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience, the various armies were ordered to shoot. Renmei stated that his strength had not declined and asked to shoot two arrows in the hall. The emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 既而前奏曰：“臣老於戎門，多戍外郡，罕曾入覲京闕。

translations.literal: He then advanced and memorialized: "Your servant has grown old in the martial gate, garrisoned many outer commanderies, and has rarely had audience at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced and said, "Your servant has grown old in military service, garrisoned many outer commanderies, and has rarely seen the capital.

sentences.zh: 前後征行，體被三十餘創，今日得對萬乘，千載之幸。

translations.literal: In campaigns before and after, my body has received more than thirty wounds; today I may face the imperial presence — a fortune of a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns before and after my body has received more than thirty wounds. Today I may face the Son of Heaven — a fortune of a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 儻或備員宿衛，立殿庭下一日足矣。

translations.literal: If perchance I might fill a post in palace guard and stand one day beneath the hall steps, that would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: If perchance I might fill a palace guard post and stand one day beneath the hall steps, that would be enough.

sentences.zh: ”上顧傅潛而笑，潛亦稱其武幹，力留，補馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: " The emperor looked at Fu Qian and smiled; Qian also praised his martial ability, and by force retained him and appointed him deputy chief commander of the horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor looked at Fu Qian and smiled. Qian also praised his martial ability and pressed to retain him, appointing him deputy chief commander of the horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 潛屯北面，常以自隨。

translations.literal: When Qian garrisoned the north he constantly kept Renmei with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian garrisoned the north he constantly kept Renmei with him.

sentences.zh: 契丹攻蒲陰，仁美領萬騎解其圍。

translations.literal: When the Khitan attacked Puyin, Renmei led ten thousand horsemen to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Puyin, Renmei led ten thousand horsemen to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 又從王超屯鎮、定、儀、渭，累遷龍衛軍都指揮使、領順州刺史，復屯鎮、定。

translations.literal: He again followed Wang Chao in garrisoning Zhen, Ding, Yi, and Wei, was repeatedly transferred to commander of the Dragon Guard and nominal prefect of Shunzhou, and again garrisoned Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Wang Chao in garrisoning Zhen, Ding, Yi, and Wei, rose to commander of the Dragon Guard and nominal prefect of Shunzhou, and again garrisoned Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 時州有亡命卒聚盜，剽村閭為患，王超委仁美招捕。

translations.literal: At the time in the prefecture fugitive soldiers gathered as bandits and plundered villages and hamlets as a scourge; Wang Chao entrusted Renmei with recruiting and capturing them.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive soldiers in the prefecture had gathered as bandits and were plundering villages. Wang Chao entrusted Renmei with capturing them.

sentences.zh: 仁美選勇敢卒，詐亡命趣賊所，得其要領，即自往諭以禍福，留賊中一日。

translations.literal: Renmei selected brave soldiers, pretended to be fugitives and hastened to the bandits' place, learned their essentials, then went himself to instruct them on fortune and disaster, and remained among the bandits one day.
translations.idiomatic: Renmei selected brave soldiers who pretended to be fugitives, learned the bandits' essentials, then went himself to lecture them on fortune and disaster and remained among them one day.

sentences.zh: 超忽失仁美，求之甚急。

translations.literal: Chao suddenly lost track of Renmei and sought him with extreme urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Chao suddenly lost track of Renmei and sought him with extreme urgency.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，仁美至，具道其事，乃出庫錢付仁美為賞。

translations.literal: At daybreak Renmei arrived, explained the whole affair in detail, and Chao thereupon took money from the storehouse and gave it to Renmei as reward.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Renmei returned, explained the whole affair, and Chao took money from the storehouse as his reward.

sentences.zh: 不數日，賊悉降，凡得二百餘人，以隸軍籍。

translations.literal: Within a few days the bandits all surrendered; in all more than two hundred were obtained and enrolled in the military rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the bandits all surrendered — more than two hundred in all — and were enrolled in the military rolls.

sentences.zh: 論曰：繼忠臨陣赴敵，以死自效，其生也亦幸而免，然在朔庭貴寵用事，議者方之李陵，而大節固已虧矣。

translations.literal: The commentators say: When Jizhong faced the battle line and rushed to the enemy, offering his death in loyal service, in life too he was fortunate to escape, yet in the northern court he was favored and held power; critics compared him to Li Ling, and his great integrity was already compromised.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Jizhong rushed to the enemy line and offered his life in loyal service. In life too he was fortunate to survive, yet in the Khitan court he was favored and held power. Critics compared him to Li Ling, and his great integrity was already compromised.

sentences.zh: 潛為三路帥，握兵八萬餘，大敵在前，逗撓畏縮，致康保裔以無援戰沒，此而不誅，宋於是乎失刑矣。

translations.literal: Qian was commander of three routes and held more than eighty thousand troops; with a great enemy before him he was dilatory, fearful, and shrank back, causing Kang Baoyin to fight and perish without relief — that this was not punished shows that Song at this point had lost the rule of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qian commanded three routes with more than eighty thousand troops. With a great enemy before him he was dilatory and shrank back, causing Kang Baoyin to fight and perish without relief. That he was not punished shows that the Song had lost the rule of punishment.

sentences.zh: 興、均輩或由藩邸進，或自行伍起，一時際會，出則書勳轅門，入則拱扈岩陛，求其如古名將，則未之見也。

translations.literal: Xing, Jun, and their kind either advanced through the princely residence or rose from the ranks; for a time they met with opportunity, and going out they inscribed merit at the camp gate while entering they attended beside the imperial steps — yet to seek in them generals like those of old, that has not been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Jun, and their kind either advanced through the princely residence or rose from the ranks. For a time they met with opportunity: going out they won merit at the camp gate, entering they attended beside the throne. Yet to find in them generals like those of antiquity — that has not been seen.
